Job Description & Summary

The Opportunity

As an Executive Concierge - PST you will provide administrative support for senior leaders, managing schedules, coordinating meetings, handling confidential information, and helping keep daily operations moving smoothly within our Internal Firm Services practice. As an Administrative professional, you will deliver efficient and effective support, build positive working relationships, stay organized, and adapt to changing priorities while handling tasks thoroughly and in a professional manner. In this role at PwC, you will support internal-facing teams by anticipating needs, organizing information, communicating clearly, and responding to shifting assignments with a steady approach.

Responsibilities

  • Managing executive calendars, prioritizing appointments, and adjusting schedules to meet shifting needs
    - Coordinating meetings, conference room logistics, and virtual sessions across time zones
    - Arranging domestic and international travel, lodging, ground transportation, and itinerary changes
    - Handling confidential information, sensitive correspondence, and executive records with discretion
    - Preparing agendas, meeting materials, briefing packets, and follow-up action summaries
    - Tracking requests, deadlines, and action items to keep work moving in an organized manner
    - Drafting, editing, and routing correspondence, presentations, and internal communications
    - Processing expenses, invoices, and administrative documents using office productivity and travel systems
    - Maintaining filing systems, records management processes, and digital document repositories
    - Supporting guest services, office coordination, and special events that contribute to smooth workplace operations

    What You Must Have

    - At least a High School Diploma or the equivalent degree
    - At least 1 years of experience

    What Sets You Apart

    - Administrative support experience in workplace or concierge services
    - Managing calendars, travel, meetings, and confidential correspondence
    - Coordinating guest services, office supplies, and records
    - Communicating clearly across varied audiences and changing priorities
    - Organizing tasks, tracking details, and adapting quickly to requests
    - Using office productivity tools, data entry, and reporting

    Travel Requirements

Up to 20%

jobs.description:
Head of Sales & Distribution – WealthTech & Investment Technology | Remote

Company: Artha
Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Industry: WealthTech / Investment Technology
Function: Sales, Distribution & Go-to-Market Leadership

About Artha

At Pavago, one of our clients, Artha, is hiring a Head of Sales & Distribution to build and lead its commercial strategy across RIAs, family offices, and institutional investors.

Artha is a portfolio intelligence platform built for financial advisors, wealth managers, family offices, and institutional investors. Its technology helps investment professionals understand how portfolios may behave as market conditions change, identify potential risks and their underlying drivers, and evaluate portfolio decisions through scenario analysis and optimization.

Artha is already live in market, with paying customers, institutional use, and integrations across the wealth-management ecosystem. The platform was built by a team with decades of experience across investment management, portfolio construction, ETFs, financial technology, product, and engineering.

The product has been built. The next chapter is about building distribution around it.

The Opportunity

This is a zero-to-one commercial leadership role for someone who has built before—not someone looking simply to manage an established sales organization.

You won’t inherit a mature inbound funnel, SDR organization, or finished sales playbook. Instead, you’ll work directly with Artha’s founders and product leadership to determine how the platform goes to market, sharpen the commercial story, identify scalable channels, and personally turn opportunities into customers.

Initially, this will be a highly hands-on role. You’ll:

  • Open doors and leverage your existing network
  • Personally prospect and generate pipeline
  • Run discovery and product conversations
  • Develop strategic relationships
  • Test positioning and messaging
  • Build direct and partnership-driven distribution channels
  • Manage opportunities through the sales cycle
  • Personally close business

What you learn from the market will directly influence Artha’s positioning, product roadmap, partnerships, and broader go-to-market strategy.

As the commercial motion becomes repeatable, you’ll have the opportunity to build the organization around it.

What You’ll Own

Sales & Distribution Strategy

  • Build and execute Artha’s sales and distribution strategy across:
    • Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs)
    • Family offices
    • Institutional investors
  • Determine the customer segments and use cases with the strongest commercial potential
  • Identify the messages and channels generating the strongest market signal
  • Develop a repeatable commercial model capable of scaling beyond founder-led selling
  • Help define Artha’s ideal customer profile and go-to-market priorities

Hands-On Sales & Pipeline Generation

  • Personally source new opportunities and open doors
  • Leverage and expand relationships across the wealth-management and investment ecosystem
  • Conduct prospecting and outbound business development
  • Run discovery conversations
  • Deliver compelling product and commercial presentations
  • Manage opportunities through the full sales cycle
  • Navigate objections and complex stakeholder conversations
  • Build and manage qualified pipeline
  • Personally negotiate and close meaningful business

This is a leadership role, but you will be selling.

Strategic Distribution & Partnerships

  • Develop both direct-sales and partnership-driven distribution
  • Build strategic relationships with:
    • Wealth platforms
    • Custodians
    • Technology providers
    • Asset managers
    • Other ecosystem partners
  • Identify partnerships capable of expanding Artha’s market reach
  • Evaluate strategic distribution opportunities based on commercial potential
  • Develop relationships into scalable distribution channels

Positioning & Commercial Narrative

  • Own the commercial narrative alongside Product, Investments, and Marketing
  • Translate sophisticated investment technology into a clear and compelling commercial story
  • Help develop and continuously refine:
    • Positioning
    • Sales collateral
    • Outbound messaging
    • Product demonstrations
    • Objection handling
    • Customer use cases
  • Use real market conversations to sharpen Artha’s messaging
  • Ensure the sales narrative resonates with sophisticated investment professionals

Sales Operations & Commercial Infrastructure

  • Establish a disciplined sales process from the ground up
  • Build CRM structure and pipeline-management standards
  • Define qualification criteria and sales stages
  • Establish KPIs and commercial reporting
  • Develop forecasting processes
  • Create a consistent sales operating cadence
  • Maintain visibility into pipeline quality, progression, and revenue opportunities
  • Build the commercial infrastructure required to support future scale

Market & Product Feedback

  • Bring structured customer and prospect feedback into Product
  • Identify recurring customer needs, objections, and use cases
  • Help Product understand where the strongest commercial demand exists
  • Translate market feedback into actionable insights
  • Work directly with founders, investment professionals, product leaders, and engineers
  • Help inform product priorities based on commercial opportunities

Commercial Leadership

  • Represent Artha at industry events, conferences, and strategic meetings
  • Establish credibility with senior stakeholders across wealth management and investment technology
  • Develop Artha’s commercial presence in the market
  • As repeatability is established, build and lead the broader commercial organization
  • Create the foundation, processes, and playbook future sales and distribution hires can scale

Requirements

  • Meaningful experience selling WealthTech, investment technology, portfolio solutions, asset-management solutions, or related financial products
  • Deep familiarity with the wealth-management and investment ecosystem
  • Established relationships across RIAs, family offices, and/or institutional investors
  • Proven track record of personally generating pipeline and closing meaningful business
  • Experience building or helping build a zero-to-one commercial motion
  • Experience developing sales strategy where a mature playbook or inbound engine did not already exist
  • Experience with both:
    • Direct sales
    • Strategic distribution partnerships
  • Ability to shape positioning, messaging, collateral, and sales processes based on market feedback
  • Ability to translate sophisticated investment products and technology into a simple, compelling commercial narrative
  • Comfortable selling directly to sophisticated investment professionals and decision-makers
  • Strong pipeline management and commercial discipline
  • Comfortable working directly with founders, investment professionals, product leaders, and engineers
  • Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort operating in ambiguity
  • Willingness to remain highly hands-on in prospecting, discovery, relationship development, and closing

Especially Valuable Experience

Experience with any of the following is particularly valuable:

  • Portfolio construction
  • Model portfolios
  • TAMPs
  • Custodial platforms
  • Investment analytics
  • Advisor technology
  • Wealth-management platforms
  • Asset-management solutions
  • Institutional investment technology
  • Financial advisor technology ecosystems

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Have built commercial motions before, rather than only managed established sales teams
  • Have a meaningful network within wealth management and investment technology
  • Know how to create pipeline without relying on a mature inbound engine
  • Can personally open doors and convert relationships into commercial opportunities
  • Are equally comfortable discussing sophisticated investment concepts and closing business
  • Can identify patterns across early customer conversations and turn them into a repeatable sales strategy
  • Understand both direct selling and strategic distribution
  • Want significant influence over positioning, customer strategy, partnerships, and product direction
  • Are comfortable working closely with founders in an early-stage environment
  • Can move between high-level commercial strategy and hands-on execution
  • Are entrepreneurial, analytical, and commercially minded
  • Want to build the sales organization—not simply inherit one

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day could include prospecting into target RIAs or family offices, leveraging your network to open a conversation with an institutional investor, running discovery with a potential customer, or presenting Artha’s portfolio intelligence platform to investment professionals.

You may then work with Product and Investments to refine positioning based on what you’re hearing in the market, review the pipeline and forecast, develop a strategic distribution relationship with a wealth platform or custodian, and prepare for an industry meeting or conference.

Early on, much of your time will be spent directly in the market. As patterns emerge, you’ll turn those learnings into a repeatable commercial process and scalable distribution model.

In short: you’ll build Artha’s commercial engine while personally proving how it works.

What Success Looks Like

Your first priority will be learning—Artha, its customers, the market, and why prospects engage or don’t.

From there, success means:

  • Sharpening Artha’s ideal customer profile and commercial narrative
  • Materially increasing qualified market conversations
  • Establishing a disciplined and measurable sales process
  • Determining which segments, channels, messages, and use cases show the strongest commercial signal
  • Building qualified pipeline
  • Converting pipeline into revenue
  • Developing meaningful strategic distribution relationships
  • Creating a repeatable distribution model
  • Reducing dependence on individual relationships and founder-led selling
  • Building the commercial foundation required for future scale

Key Metrics for Success

  • Qualified market conversations generated
  • Qualified pipeline created
  • Pipeline-to-revenue conversion
  • New customers closed
  • Revenue generated
  • Sales-cycle progression and velocity
  • Strategic distribution relationships established
  • Direct-sales channel performance
  • Partner-driven pipeline and opportunities
  • CRM and forecasting discipline
  • Identification of repeatable customer segments and use cases
  • Commercial messaging effectiveness
  • Development of a scalable sales and distribution model

Why Artha, Why Now

Artha isn’t asking you to sell an idea that still needs to be built.

The technology is live. The investment expertise is established. There are real customers, institutional use, and industry integrations. The platform addresses an everyday challenge for investment professionals: understanding what changing markets could mean for their portfolios.

What hasn’t been built yet is the commercial engine capable of taking Artha to a much larger market.

That’s the opportunity.

You’ll join early enough to have genuine influence over positioning, customer strategy, partnerships, product, and the future commercial organization, while working with an established platform and experienced team.

For someone who has spent years in wealth management or investment technology thinking, “I know how I’d build this if I had the opportunity,” this role provides that opportunity.

Compensation

Base Salary + Significant Performance-Based Incentive Compensation + Equity Opportunity

Compensation will reflect the seniority of the role and the expectation that this person will both build and personally execute Artha’s commercial strategy.

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application
  2. Spark Hire One-Way Video Interview
  3. Interview with Pavago
  4. Artha Founder / Leadership Interview
  5. Final Interview
  6. Offer & Onboarding

Spark Hire Video Interview – Required

As part of the application process, all candidates are required to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire.

After completing the first step of your application, you’ll receive a Spark Hire invitation by email with instructions to record and submit your video responses.

Completion of the Spark Hire video is required to be considered for the next stage. Please check your inbox as well as your spam or junk folder for the invitation.

Apply Now

If you’re an experienced wealth-management or investment-technology commercial leader who has built sales motions from the ground up, personally generated and closed meaningful business, and developed relationships across RIAs, family offices, institutional investors, and strategic distribution partners, we’d love to hear from you.

This is an opportunity to take a proven investment technology platform and build the commercial engine around it from zero to one.

The Senior Manager, Technical Project Management provides cross-site or platform-level technical leadership for strategic capital programs and project delivery. This role leads the most consequential investments, develops common engineering approaches and governance, and influences network capital strategy, technology deployment, supplier models, and project execution capability.


This position reports to the Director of Engineering Project Management and is part of the Global Operations Engineering team. This will be a remote position, preferably near or in close proximity to an airport for travel.

  • Lead the selection, governance, and performance of strategic engineering partners, OEMs, and integrators, establishing technical and commercial models that improve execution speed, standardization, quality, and total installed cost.
  • Drive standardization and replication of proven equipment, utilities, automation, facility solutions, engineering standards, and lessons learned across the manufacturing network while enabling justified site-specific adaptation.

The essential requirements of the job include:

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:

  • PMP or equivalent advanced project or program credential; an advanced engineering or business degree may be beneficial but is not required.
  • Experience with global or multi-site capital programs, strategic supplier governance, standardized design platforms, and major facility or manufacturing expansions.
  • Recognized expertise in one or more project domains such as regulated facilities, utilities, automation, manufacturing equipment, laboratories, packaging, or site infrastructure.

jobs.excerpt: “I am hugely excited about my future and the future of CyberOne.
jobs.description:
“I am hugely excited about my future and the future of CyberOne. I have enjoyed my time here immensely and have learnt a huge amount in a short space of time, year-for-year I've learnt more here than I have at Microsoft and PwC.” - CyberOne Consultant

About CyberOne

CyberOne is a pure-play Microsoft security partner dedicated to helping enterprises realise the full value of the Microsoft Security portfolio—across Defender XDR, Sentinel, Entra, Purview, Intune, Copilot for Security and more. We combine deep technical expertise with outcome-driven services that accelerate secure cloud adoption, modernise threat protection and simplify compliance.

Job Title:Incident Response Lead

Location:Remote

Employment Type:Full time

Role purpose

The Cyber Incident Response (CIR) Lead is responsible for delivering CyberOne’s incident response engagements as part of a pool of CIR Leads, leading clients and technical teams through the investigation, containment and recovery of cyber security incidents.

The role combines incident leadership, technical judgement and clear stakeholder communication to minimise business impact and support informed decisions under pressure.

Responsibilities

  • Lead cyber incident response engagements from initial assessment and mobilisation through to recovery, reporting and post-incident review.
  • Establish the incident’s severity, known scope, business impact and immediate priorities, maintaining an accurate assessment as new evidence emerges.
  • Coordinate internal technical teams, client teams and third-party providers, setting clear actions, owners and deadlines.
  • Lead war room meetings and maintain an appropriate communication cadence, providing clear updates to technical teams, senior management and board-level stakeholders.
  • Translate technical findings into business risks, response options and recommendations, clearly distinguishing confirmed facts, working hypotheses and evidence gaps.
  • Coordinate containment, eradication and recovery activities, ensuring recommendations consider operational dependencies, evidence preservation and the client’s approval requirements.
  • Maintain incident timelines, decision logs, action trackers and handover records to support continuity and accountability.
  • Deliver engagements within the agreed scope and service commitments, escalating capacity constraints, delivery risks and additional requirements to the Head of Incident Response.
  • Produce and quality-assure investigation reports and post-incident reviews, ensuring conclusions are supported by evidence and recommendations are practical and prioritised.
  • Support client preparedness through incident response plan reviews, onboarding workshops and tabletop exercises.
  • Provide mentoring to SecOps team members in training to be cross disciplined responders.
  • Contribute improvements to playbooks, templates and delivery processes using lessons identified during engagements.

Essential professional requirements

  • Demonstrable experience leading significant cyber security incidents, including coordinating technical response activities and managing client communications.
  • Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams during high-pressure situations, including where responders do not report directly to the role.
  • Confident communication with executive and board-level stakeholders, including explaining uncertainty, operational risk and difficult response decisions.
  • Strong judgement and prioritisation, with the ability to make timely recommendations using incomplete information and escalate decisions appropriately.
  • Experience managing stakeholder expectations and maintaining constructive relationships during disruptive or sensitive incidents.
  • Excellent written communication, with experience producing clear incident reports, executive summaries and actionable remediation recommendations.
  • Strong organisational discipline, including maintaining accurate records, managing competing priorities and providing effective handovers.
  • Professional discretion and sound judgement when handling sensitive client information and investigation evidence.

Essential technical requirements

  • Practical experience responding to incidents such as ransomware, business email compromise, identity compromise, malware infections and suspected data exfiltration.
  • Strong understanding of incident response activities, including preparation, detection, investigation, containment, eradication, recovery and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to assess and challenge technical findings, identify gaps in an investigation and direct further analysis to establish scope, attack progression and business impact.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise environments, including Windows, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, cloud services and common network technologies.
  • Experience using SIEM, EDR and identity telemetry to support investigations, including correlating activity across endpoints, accounts and cloud services.
  • Understanding of attacker techniques involving credential theft, session compromise, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement and command-and-control communications.
  • Ability to evaluate containment and recovery options, including their operational consequences, dependencies and potential effects on evidence.
  • Understanding of evidence preservation, secure evidence handling and chain-of-custody principles, including recognising when specialist forensic support is required.
  • Ability to recognise telemetry, retention and licensing limitations and explain how these affect investigative confidence and conclusions.
  • Practical understanding of incident response guidance and threat frameworks, particularly NIST SP 800-61 and MITRE ATT&CK.

Desirable experience and qualifications

  • Experience delivering incident response within a consultancy, managed security service provider or other client-facing environment.
  • Experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR and KQL, alongside familiarity with other enterprise security platforms.
  • Experience delivering incident preparedness workshops, tabletop exercises and post-incident reviews.
  • Experience coordinating with legal advisers, cyber insurers, specialist forensic providers and crisis communications teams.
  • Awareness of data protection and regulatory considerations, including recognising when clients require legal or privacy advice.
  • Relevant qualifications such as GCIH, GCFA, CISSP or CISM. Equivalent practical experience is equally valued.
  • ITIL 4 knowledge or certification, particularly in relation to incident, problem and change management.

Accountability and authority

The Cyber Incident Response Lead is accountable for the coordination, quality and communication of assigned engagements within agreed scope and delegated authority.

The Head of Incident Response retains accountability for the overall service, including strategy, budgets, staffing, commercial commitments and service governance.

Clients retain authority for business risk acceptance, operational changes, recovery approval and legal or regulatory decisions. The Cyber Incident Response Lead provides the information and recommendations needed to support those decisions.

jobs.description:
About Covalent

Covalent is a workforce operations platform built for complex manufacturers. We help aerospace, defense, automotive, and industrial enterprises train, qualify, deploy, and optimize frontline labor at scale.

Our software enables manufacturers to digitize workforce capability management, improve workforce readiness, and make better labor decisions using real operational data. Covalent is trusted by leading global manufacturers to connect workforce capability with production execution—turning workforce data into a strategic operational asset.

We are a profitable, growing SaaS company serving some of the world's most sophisticated manufacturing organizations. The aircraft, engines, and defense systems our customers build depend on a skilled, qualified workforce. We help make sure that the workforce is ready.

The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Enterprise Customer Success Manager to own and grow relationships with some of Covalent's largest and most strategically important customers, including two of the largest aerospace and propulsion manufacturers in the United States.

Our customers value partners who understand the complexities of their industry and the challenges they face every day. The ideal candidate can engage just as confidently with frontline manufacturing teams on the plant floor as with senior executives in the boardroom, translating operational challenges into strategic business conversations.

As part of a growing SaaS company, you'll work directly with senior leadership and have a meaningful opportunity to shape how we manage and grow our strategic enterprise accounts.

What You'll Do

Strategic Account Management & Executive Engagement

  • Own the overall success of a portfolio of Covalent's largest enterprise customers, developing strategic account plans aligned with their business objectives and long-term priorities.
  • Proactively establish and strengthen relationships beyond day-to-day operational contacts, engaging directors, vice presidents, executive sponsors, and key decision-makers across facilities and business units.
  • Lead executive business reviews and strategic planning discussions that demonstrate measurable business outcomes, reinforce Covalent's value, and identify future opportunities.

Customer Value & Business Outcomes

  • Develop a deep understanding of each customer's manufacturing operations, strategic priorities, and workforce challenges, including operator qualification and certification, audit readiness, and production readiness across facilities.
  • Translate Covalent's capabilities into measurable business outcomes, including workforce readiness, operational efficiency, training effectiveness, and improved labor utilization.
  • Leverage customer data, product analytics, and operational insights to quantify business impact, communicate return on investment, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor, connecting Covalent's technology to broader operational and strategic initiatives rather than focusing solely on product adoption.

Retention, Expansion & Growth

  • Own customer health, retention, and long-term account growth, proactively identifying risks and developing mitigation strategies.
  • Identify and develop expansion opportunities across additional facilities, business units, use cases, and enterprise initiatives.
  • Partner with internal leadership and commercial teams to develop account growth strategies, support renewal discussions, and strengthen Covalent's position within key accounts.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Customer Advocacy

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Professional Services, and Support to ensure customer priorities are understood and critical initiatives are successfully executed.
  • Maintain oversight of important implementations, integrations, escalations, and customer initiatives, coordinating internal resources and driving accountability.
  • Represent the voice of the customer internally while contributing ideas and best practices that help strengthen Covalent's strategic account management approach as we scale.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Relevant Industry Experience: Direct experience in aerospace, defense, or regulated industrial manufacturing, either working within a manufacturer (operations, quality, training, manufacturing engineering, or related functions) or supporting manufacturers as a primary customer base.
  • Enterprise Account Experience: 5+ years of relevant experience in enterprise customer success, account management, or customer-facing manufacturing roles, with demonstrated responsibility for complex enterprise relationships or initiatives.
  • Executive Engagement: Demonstrated ability to establish credibility and build relationships with senior leaders, including directors, vice presidents, and executive decision-makers.
  • Strategic Business Acumen: Ability to understand complex operational challenges, connect technology or process improvements to business objectives, and communicate measurable value.
  • Account Growth & Relationship Development: Experience identifying opportunities to expand relationships, increase organizational engagement, or drive broader adoption of solutions and initiatives.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Proven ability to navigate complex organizations, align multiple stakeholders, and drive initiatives involving internal and external teams.
  • Communication & Ownership: Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to independently manage competing priorities while maintaining accountability for customer outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing strategic enterprise accounts within a B2B SaaS organization, particularly with aerospace and defense manufacturers, OEMs, or their supplier ecosystems.
  • Familiarity with workforce qualification, compliance, manufacturing operations, or production readiness in regulated environments.
  • Experience working across multiple manufacturing facilities, divisions, or global operations.
  • Knowledge of enterprise technology ecosystems, including HRIS, LMS, ERP, MES, or workforce management platforms.
  • Demonstrated success expanding software or operational initiatives from individual facilities into broader enterprise adoption.

Benefits

The aircraft, engines, and defense systems our customers build depend on a skilled, qualified workforce. Covalent helps make sure that workforce is ready, and in this role you'll see that impact firsthand, working directly with some of the most sophisticated aerospace and defense manufacturers in the world.

jobs.excerpt: About Bask HealthBask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a User Researcher, Merchant Operations to help Bask Health better understand how merchants manage their day-to-day business operations through our software platform.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform brings together merchant tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce capabilities.

As a User Researcher, Merchant Operations, you'll investigate how business owners and operational teams use Bask Health to complete administrative tasks, manage workflows, resolve issues, and keep their businesses running efficiently.

This is a hands-on research role focused on understanding real operational behavior rather than evaluating individual interface screens in isolation.

You'll study how merchants organize their work, move between different areas of the platform, interpret operational information, and coordinate tasks involving multiple systems or stakeholders.

Your research may involve merchant dashboards, order-related workflows, subscription management, product configuration, account administration, reporting, and other operational tools.

You'll investigate where merchants encounter unnecessary steps, repetitive work, confusing processes, or limitations that make routine tasks more difficult.

A major part of this role will involve understanding how merchants complete work in practice. You'll conduct interviews, observe workflows, and evaluate how users interact with the platform during everyday business activities.

You'll also study differences between merchant segments. A small business owner managing operations independently may have different needs than an established organization with multiple team members and more specialized responsibilities.

You'll work closely with product managers to define research priorities and identify operational problems worth investigating.

You'll collaborate with product designers to evaluate workflows, improve task organization, and simplify administrative experiences.

You'll partner with engineers to understand technical constraints, system behavior, and opportunities to reduce unnecessary manual work.

You'll also collaborate with Customer Success and support teams to understand recurring merchant issues, common operational questions, and areas where merchants require additional assistance.

Because Bask supports healthcare-related businesses, operational workflows may involve connections between merchant activities, patient experiences, and authorized clinical or pharmacy processes. You'll research these interactions while respecting user permissions, privacy requirements, and professional boundaries.

You'll use qualitative research, usability testing, available behavioral data, and operational feedback to develop a detailed understanding of how merchants work.

You'll translate your findings into actionable recommendations that help product teams improve workflow efficiency, reduce friction, and support merchants as their businesses grow.

We're looking for someone who enjoys understanding how businesses operate, is comfortable researching complex software workflows, and can turn detailed observations into practical product improvements.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct user research focused on Bask Health's merchant operations and administrative workflows.
  • Study how merchants manage day-to-day business activities through the platform.
  • Conduct interviews with business owners, administrators, and authorized operational users.
  • Observe how merchants complete recurring tasks and manage operational responsibilities.
  • Research merchant dashboards and administrative interfaces.
  • Evaluate order-related workflows and operational status management.
  • Study subscription management and recurring commerce administration.
  • Research product configuration and ongoing catalog maintenance.
  • Evaluate account administration, user permissions, and team workflows.
  • Investigate reporting and business monitoring experiences.
  • Identify repetitive tasks, unnecessary steps, and workflow inefficiencies.
  • Research how merchants move between different platform tools to complete tasks.
  • Study operational handoffs involving merchants and other authorized stakeholders.
  • Develop research plans, interview guides, and workflow observation materials.
  • Create workflow maps and task analyses that document how merchants complete work.
  • Conduct usability studies for administrative tools and operational interfaces.
  • Evaluate prototypes for proposed workflow improvements.
  • Identify differences in operational needs across merchant segments.
  • Collaborate with Customer Success teams to identify recurring merchant challenges.
  • Review support feedback and operational observations to inform research priorities.
  • Partner with product managers to define operational research questions.
  • Work with product designers to simplify complex administrative workflows.
  • Collaborate with engineers to understand technical constraints and system behavior.
  • Incorporate available product analytics into research findings.
  • Analyze qualitative data to identify recurring operational patterns.
  • Develop actionable recommendations for improving task efficiency and usability.
  • Present research findings to product, design, engineering, and relevant operational teams.
  • Maintain organized research documentation and reusable workflow insights.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in user research, UX research, product research, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or case studies demonstrating research for digital products.
  • Experience conducting research involving business software or complex operational workflows.
  • Strong understanding of qualitative research methods.
  • Experience conducting user interviews and usability studies.
  • Ability to observe and analyze how users complete real-world tasks.
  • Experience developing research plans and study objectives.
  • Familiarity with workflow mapping and task analysis.
  • Ability to identify operational friction and process inefficiencies.
  • Experience evaluating administrative interfaces or complex web applications.
  • Strong analytical and qualitative synthesis skills.
  • Ability to translate research findings into actionable product recommendations.
  • Experience collaborating with product managers and product designers.
  • Ability to communicate findings to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with product discovery and iterative development processes.
  • Understanding of information architecture and interaction design principles.
  • Experience researching workflows involving multiple steps or user roles.
  • Familiarity with participant recruitment and screening.
  • Understanding of research ethics and informed consent.
  • Experience incorporating customer feedback into research activities.
  • Familiarity with quantitative data and product analytics.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and research quality.
  • Ability to manage multiple research priorities.
  • Ability to independently deliver research projects in a cross-functional environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience researching B2B SaaS platforms.
  • Familiarity with merchant operations and business management software.
  • Experience conducting research for e-commerce platforms.
  • Understanding of Shopify or comparable commerce ecosystems.
  • Experience researching order management and fulfillment-related workflows.
  • Familiarity with subscription management and recurring billing processes.
  • Understanding of merchant reporting and operational dashboards.
  • Experience researching administrative workflows involving multiple user roles.
  • Familiarity with account permissions and team management interfaces.
  • Experience studying operational handoffs between different teams or systems.
  • Understanding of white-label or multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
  • Background in healthcare technology or telehealth platforms.
  • Familiarity with healthcare-related operational processes.
  • Experience collaborating with Customer Success or implementation teams.
  • Familiarity with tools such as UserTesting, Maze, Dovetail, or comparable research platforms.
  • Experience evaluating Figma prototypes.
  • Understanding of mixed-methods research approaches.
  • Experience combining qualitative research with product analytics.
  • Familiarity with service blueprinting and operational journey mapping.
  • Experience working in fast-moving, cross-functional product teams.

About NLA and TCS

New Left Accelerator (NLA) and its 501(c)(3) affiliate, The Capacity Shop (TCS), lead operational capacity-building programs that empower social justice organizations and movements to execute bold work safely. We bridge the gap between ambitious strategy and operational excellence, scaling structures and impact without sacrificing legal compliance or integrity. To achieve systemic change, organizations must use every tool in their toolbox effectively—including multi-entity structures.

Through deep collaboration with field experts, we build the financial and compliance training systems that allow movement organizations to manage risk and remain resilient. Our work is rooted in a commitment to:

  • Power Building For Systemic Change: Equipping organizations to build power to dismantle oppressive structures.
  • Operational Power: Building the "operational" capacity to execute bold work and to strategically manage risk.
  • A Multi-Entity Lens: Optimizing the diverse legal structures necessary to win critical battles.
  • Transformative Partnerships: Prioritizing those working at the intersections of race, gender, and class.

At NLA, our work is guided by a Theory of Change. We accompany organizations and movements in building sustainable, resilient ecosystems prepared to win the most ambitious fights of our time.

Role Overview

NLA is seeking a highly organized, thoughtful, and proactive Senior Executive Assistant. This is a full-time position that will provide dedicated, high-level support to the Executive Director, including: extensive calendar management, Board logistics, executive communications, and project management. This position will serve as a key operational and communications partner to the Executive Director, helping manage priorities, coordinating travel and engagements, preparing communications and meeting materials, and ensuring follow through. We are seeking candidates with significant experience, particularly within multi-entity, nonprofit movement-building organizations.

We are a remote (U.S.-based) organization. Proximity to the Bay Area in California is preferred.

Responsibilities

ED & Leadership Team Project Management

Calendar Management & Engagement Support

Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. Social media will be a major focus, including corporate and executive content on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and other relevant platforms. The Director will establish the strategy for these channels, develop recognizable executive voices, and connect social storytelling with deeper content on the corporate blog and other owned platforms. The position combines strategic leadership with hands-on writing, editing, and execution. The Director will lead content specialists, manage agency, freelance, and creative partners. jobs.title: Google Ads Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

jobs.title: Senior Google Ads Buyer, DTC eCommerce
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

UX/UI Designer

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a UX/UI Designer to create polished, user-centered experiences for Venveo's digital products.

This role combines strong visual design with UX thinking, research, prototyping, and design system work. You’ll collaborate closely with product managers, developers, and other stakeholders to translate requirements into high-quality designs and ensure those designs are implemented accurately.

What You’ll Own

Interface Design

  • Create polished, user-centered UI designs for Venveo's digital products.
  • Translate briefs and wireframes into high-quality, production-ready visuals.
  • Ensure designs align with established design systems and brand standards.

UX Research & Validation

  • Conduct or support user research activities, including usability testing and heuristic reviews.
  • Synthesize research findings to inform design decisions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the user experience.

Prototyping & Iteration

  • Build interactive prototypes at the appropriate level of fidelity.
  • Use prototypes to communicate concepts and gather stakeholder feedback.
  • Iterate quickly toward validated design solutions.

Design System Stewardship

  • Contribute to and maintain Venveo's component library and design system.
  • Ensure consistency across product surfaces.
  • Help reduce design debt over time.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with product managers, developers, and other stakeholders.
  • Align on requirements and define appropriate scope.
  • Ensure designs are technically feasible and accurately implemented.

Handoff & Developer Support

  • Prepare precise design specifications and assets for engineering handoff.
  • Remain available during development to answer design-related questions.
  • Review implementations and provide feedback on design fidelity.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Demonstrated professional experience in UX/UI design.
  • Portfolio showing end-to-end product thinking and strong visual craft.
  • Proficiency in Figma, including component creation, auto-layout, prototyping, and design system management.
  • Solid understanding of UX fundamentals, including information architecture, user flows, interaction design, and accessibility best practices.
  • Experience working in cross-functional product teams alongside engineers and product managers.
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate asynchronously and clearly present design rationale.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You take ownership when requirements are incomplete or ambiguous.
  • You ask the right questions, make reasonable assumptions explicit, and keep work moving forward.
  • You maintain a high standard for visual quality while remaining open to feedback.
  • You treat critique as useful input and separate feedback on the work from personal judgment.
  • You communicate proactively across time zones and surface blockers early.
  • You balance speed and craft, knowing when to move quickly and when a design decision requires deeper exploration.
  • You keep collaborators informed without needing to be prompted.

What Success Looks Like

  • Digital product interfaces are polished, user-centered, and aligned with established design standards.
  • User flows and interaction patterns are clear and thoughtfully designed.
  • Prototypes effectively communicate concepts and support validation.
  • Design system components remain consistent and well maintained.
  • Engineering teams receive clear, accurate specifications and assets.
  • Implemented designs closely match approved designs.
  • Collaboration remains proactive, clear, and effective across product and engineering teams.

Typical Day

Your day will likely begin with a review of async feedback from Venveo teammates on current design files, responding with annotations or updated iterations in Figma.

Mid-morning may involve a short sync with a product manager or engineer to align on requirements for an upcoming feature. From there, you may move into focused design work, refining user flows, producing high-fidelity screens, or building new components for the design system.

Later in the day, you might hand off a completed specification to the development team, run a quick usability check on a prototype, or review a developer implementation and flag any discrepancies.

The role is predominantly async, so clear written communication in every deliverable matters as much as the designs themselves.

  3. Final Selection

Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.


Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.


Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.


As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.


We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.


Collectors is seeking a Capital Markets Compliance Lead to build the governance, oversight and integrity of its market-facing activity across grading, custody, pricing data and marketplaces. You will report to the Head of Risk & Compliance and work closely with Legal, Product, Engineering, Finance and business leaders.


Our businesses sit unusually close to the market: we authenticate, store, price, publish data about and help sell the assets themselves. We hold our market conduct to a capital-markets standard because collectors and partners make financial decisions based on our grades, prices and custody. This role is strategic: you will design and inspect controls and set the standard.

What You'll Do

Build a firm-wide markets compliance framework that is risk-based, auditable and scalable, and keep it current as our product set grows. Understand how our roles as grader, custodian, data and index publisher, and marketplace operator interact while documenting and implementing controls around each of those roles.


Market Integrity and Information Controls:

  • Design the controls around market-sensitive, non-public information: grading and population data before release, pricing and index changes, vault holdings and transaction activity. This includes wall-crossing, restricted and watch lists, access controls and escalation, treated with the seriousness of a securities-market information barrier.
  • Own the employee and insider trading framework for relevant assets: pre-clearance, personal-trading and holdings rules, blackout periods, attestations, surveillance and escalation. Align with Legal and HR and the existing employee market participation policy.
  • Oversee conflict-of-interest management across all of our roles, including vendor solutions, and report it to executives and the board as necessary.
  • Lead internal investigations of suspected misuse, working with Legal and Employee Relations.

Pricing, Index and Data Governance:

  • Build the governance framework for the prices, valuations and indexes we publish: methodology, change control, error handling, complaints and conflicts.
  • Design and implement controls over how partners and licensees use Collectors grades, prices and data in their own marketing. Much of this is rigorous documentation.
  • Review data and pricing products, licensing and marketing for accuracy, fairness and regulatory risk, including claims about performance, accuracy and ratings.
  • Embed controls over data quality and pricing inputs where people rely on them to make financial decisions.

Transactions and Fair Dealing:

  • Design the compliance program for the transactions we facilitate: fair-dealing standards, pricing and disclosure, what we are obliged to deliver, and settlement controls.
  • Address the risk of self-dealing and side-dealing: trading ahead, principal versus agent conflicts, undisclosed interests, and staff or affiliate participation.

Products, Partners and the Business

  • Provide compliance input into new products and features from inception, with a fast new-product review that gives product teams a clear answer with documented conditions.
  • Work with Legal and outside counsel on regulatory questions, and turn their conclusions into operating controls.
  • Run due diligence and ongoing oversight of commercial and data partners, including review of their marketing and disclosures.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, including teaching executives how well-run market businesses manage conduct risk, what regulators look for, and what has to be true before a new product ships.
  • Be a systems thinker: automate monitoring, attestations, testing and reporting wherever regulation allows, so the program is data-driven and scales without headcount.
  • Build and develop a markets compliance team over time. Produce reporting for executive and board audiences on conflicts, attestations, exceptions, testing and open issues.

Who You Are

  • 8+ years in markets, capital markets or investment compliance experience at an exchange, trading platform, broker-dealer, asset manager, or index or market-data provider. A broad alternative-assets or digital-assets platform is a strong fit.
  • Deep hands-on experience with MNPI, information barriers and wall-crossing, restricted and watch lists, pre-clearance, personal-trading surveillance and code-of-ethics programs.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. securities and markets regulation and of marketing and communications standards, the judgment to apply them by analogy where they do not strictly reach, and the instinct to bring in counsel at the right time.
  • Understanding of trading mechanics, market microstructure, fair dealing and principal versus agent conflicts.
  • Experience reviewing investment marketing, disclosures, and data or research products.
  • Familiarity with surveillance technology and data-driven monitoring.
  • Experience building a program in a business adopting market-conduct standards for the first time; treats controls as how we get to yes.
  • Can explain regulatory expectations to senior executives and coach non-specialists, with results you can describe with numbers (for example exam findings closed, program coverage, review turnaround).

jobs.description:
Overview

  • World Business Lenders (WBL) is a privately held portfolio lender specializing in real estate-secured business loans for underserved businesses. WBL operates with a fully remote, multinational workforce and an experienced executive leadership team.
  • Typically, the work schedule is from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, though additional hours may be required based on business needs.

About the Role

  • The Valuation Quality Control/Review Appraiser will serve as a subject matter expert in residential or commercial real estate appraisal. The role is responsible for reviewing appraisals and other valuation reports prepared by internal analysts and third-party providers, identifying material deficiencies, and recommending property values to the appropriate committee.
  • This position is focused on appraisal review, quality control, collateral risk assessment, and communication of clear, supportable valuation recommendations. It also entails producing appraisals from start to finish.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistently delivers accurate, timely, and defensible valuation recommendations.
  • Identifies material appraisal deficiencies and effectively communicates collateral risks.
  • Provides clear, well-supported recommendations to credit and investment committees.
  • Maintains high-quality, consistent appraisal review standards and supports junior analysts.

What You'll Be Doing (Core Responsibilities)

    • Review residential or commercial appraisals, evaluations, broker price opinions, automated valuation models, inspections, and related valuation reports.
    • Assess the accuracy, completeness, credibility, and suitability of each report for its intended use.
    • Evaluate property characteristics, highest and best use, zoning, market conditions, comparable selection, adjustments, income assumptions, capitalization rates, cost estimates, and value reconciliation.
    • Identify unsupported assumptions, mathematical errors, stale data, weak comparables, excessive adjustments, material omissions, and other valuation deficiencies.
    • Return deficient reports for correction, clarification, or additional support.
    • Develop an independent recommendation of property value based on the appraisal, supporting market evidence, internal records, inspections, and other available information.
    • Recommend acceptance, modification, rejection, or further investigation of submitted valuation conclusions.
    • Prepare concise written summaries of findings, risks, and recommended values.
    • Present valuation recommendations to Investment Committee, Asset Resolution Committee, Initial Credit Review Committee or other decision-making committees.
    • Explain valuation methodology, assumptions, market evidence, and collateral risks to management and committee members.
    • Recommend additional appraisals, inspections, environmental reports, engineering studies, or other analysis when existing information is insufficient.
    • Review work completed by junior analysts and provide technical guidance on appraisal methodology, comparable analysis, adjustments, and report documentation.

Requirements

  • Education
    • Bachelor’s degree in real estate, finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field.
  • Required Experience
    • 7+ years of experience in real estate appraisal, appraisal review, collateral valuation, underwriting, credit, asset management, or a related field.
    • Demonstrated experience reviewing both residential and commercial real estate appraisals.
    • Strong knowledge of the sales comparison, income capitalization, and cost approaches.
    • Experience evaluating comparable selection, market adjustments, income and expense assumptions, capitalization rates, highest and best use, and value reconciliation.
    • Experience with distressed, transitional, nonperforming, foreclosed, or complex real estate.
    • Strong analytical, written, verbal, and presentation skills.
    • Ability to exercise independent judgment and challenge unsupported valuation conclusions.
    • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, public records, property databases, listing platforms, mapping systems, and market research tools.
    • State Certified General Real Estate Appraiser credential.
    • MAI, SRA, AI-GRS, ASA, MRICS, or another recognized appraisal designation.
  • Key Performance Measures
    • Accuracy and defensibility of valuation recommendations
    • Quality and timeliness of appraisal reviews
    • Identification of material appraisal deficiencies
    • Consistency with appraisal review standards
    • Quality of committee presentations and written recommendations
    • Variance between recommended values and subsequent transaction outcomes
  • Remote Work Requirements
    • Stable, reliable internet connection.
    • Professional and dedicated remote working environment.
  • Preferred Background / Industry Experience
    • Real estate appraisal or appraisal review, particularly residential and commercial properties.
    • Commercial real estate lending, mortgage lending, credit underwriting, or collateral risk management.
    • Asset management, special assets, distressed debt, foreclosure, or REO involving complex or transitional real estate.
    • Experience with portfolio lenders, banks, private credit, or other financial institutions.
    • Experience supporting credit/investment committees, loan workouts, property dispositions, or other decisions involving real estate collateral.
  • Key Soft Skills
    • Strong analytical judgment and professional skepticism.
    • Confidence to challenge appraisers, analysts, and internal stakeholders when conclusions are not adequately supported.
    • Ability to make sound decisions when property information is incomplete or conflicting.
    • Clear and concise written and verbal communication.
    • Ability to explain complex valuation issues to non-appraisers and senior executives.
    • Strong attention to detail without losing sight of the overall collateral risk.
    • Comfortable defending a valuation recommendation in a committee environment.
    • Collaborative coaching style when reviewing the work of junior analysts.
    • High degree of independence, integrity, and objectivity
  • Specific Technical Skills Needed
    • Expert understanding of residential and commercial real estate appraisal.
    • Strong command of the Sales Comparison and Income Capitalization approach.
    • Ability to critically evaluate comparable selection and appraisal adjustments.
    • Ability to analyze rents, operating expenses, NOI, capitalization rates, discount rates, and income-based valuations.
    • Strong understanding of highest and best use, zoning, property condition, marketability, and location considerations.
    • Ability to identify appraisal errors, unsupported assumptions, inconsistencies, and material data gaps.
    • Experience reviewing distressed, nonperforming, foreclosed, transitional, or otherwise complex collateral preferred.
    • Working knowledge of USPAP and applicable appraisal independence and regulatory standards.
    • Proficiency with Excel, public property records, MLS/listing information, mapping tools, commercial real estate databases, and other valuation research resources.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Enjoy Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Work from the comfort of your own home – fully remote
  • Compensation paid in USD

What You'll Own

  • Strategy and execution across Google Search, Demand Gen, YouTube, and Microsoft audience and native inventory, MSN included.

We’re proud to be a Great Place To Work® certified company, where satisfaction, growth, and flexibility are our way of working.

We are looking for a detail-oriented Group Accountant to join our Group Finance Team and support the accurate and timely financial reporting of E&C's entities.

You’ll own key month‑end activities: from posting close entries to balance‑sheet and intercompany reconciliations. Help review the monthly numbers to spot anything that doesn’t add up. You’ll work hand‑in‑hand with our Internal Accountant, Financial Controller and external accounting/tax partners to make sure reporting is accurate, complete and on time. It’s a hands‑on role for someone who knows double‑entry and accrual accounting, enjoys digging into financial data like a number detective, and takes pride in owning and resolving discrepancies.

You’ll start by owning a few specific entities and accounting areas and getting to know the numbers inside out. We’re looking for someone curious and analytical who can read what a balance or transaction really means, flag anything that looks off, and chase it down until it’s fixed. As you settle in, there’s plenty of room to grow: take on more entities, tackle trickier accounting issues, and broaden your role in group financial reporting.

  • Issue resolution: Investigate accounting discrepancies and outstanding items and work collaboratively with the wider Group Finance Team and external partners to ensure they are appropriately resolved

  • Group-wide consistency: Help ensure that accounting treatments, close procedures and supporting documentation are applied consistently across E&C’s entities

Job Requisition ID #
