  1. Bachelor’s degree in a related field. Continuous learning, as defined by the Company’s learning philosophy, is required. Certification or progress toward certification is highly preferred and encouraged.
  2. Three (3) years of experience in a workers’ compensation claims environment which provides the necessary skills, knowledge and abilities, such as experience in reviewing, investigating and closing workers’ compensation claims. Experience of handling claims in multiple jurisdictions preferred.Bilingual skills preferred.
    1. OR
  3. One (1) year of AF Group Claims Representative I experience that includes handling of difficult or complex claims.

QUALIFICATIONS

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  3. Knowledge of workers’ compensation laws and regulations, including jurisdictional laws.
  4. Effective oral and written communication skills.
  5. Effective customer service skills.
  6. Ability to negotiate, build consensus and resolve conflict.
  7. Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet established deadlines.
  8. Attention to detail and analytical skills.
  9. Ability to work independently as well as within a team.

Job Title: Head of Channel Sales & Alliances

Location: United States, Remote

This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

Revenue is complex, and clarity is rare. Our mission at Salesloft is to transform revenue complexity into clear, decisive action for every team driving growth.

We’re building the industry’s first Predictive Revenue System, where humans and AI work together to make confident decisions based on real signals. Thousands of customers run on our platforms every day, which gives us Revenue Context: a view into what happens in a deal, when, and with what outcome.

Our vision is a future where revenue growth is predictable and the teams driving it are unstoppable. If you want to help build it, alongside people who Move as One and let Evidence over Ego guide the work, we’d love to meet you.

THE OPPORTUNITYOwn the partner channel that sources a meaningful share of Salesloft’s new closed-won revenue.

As our Head of Channel Sales & Alliances, you'll build and run a quota-carrying Channel Sales & Alliances organization focused on four motions: private equity partnerships, cloud marketplace and strategic platform alliances, ISV and MCP partnerships, and VAR, BPO, and services partnerships. The primary measure is closed-won revenue sourced through partners, supported by partner-influenced revenue and the retention and expansion of partner-sourced customers. Relationships, programs, and pipelines are critical in producing signed deals. You will be the executive face of Salesloft to our most strategic partners and the owner of the plan, the team, and the results.

On a day-to-day basis, you will:

Private Equity Partnerships

  • Build relationships with private equity firms and their operating partners to position Salesloft as the revenue platform for their portfolio companies.
  • Structure portfolio-wide agreements and programs that turn a firm-level relationship into sourced, closed-won deals across multiple portfolio companies.
  • Work with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to run portfolio-specific plays, from the initial introduction through close.

Cloud Marketplace and Strategic Platform Alliances

jobs.excerpt: The Opportunity Purdue Global is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking Compliance Officer to provide leadership for the university’s compliance, ethics, and enterprise risk management programs.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Purdue Global is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking Compliance Officer to provide leadership for the university’s compliance, ethics, and enterprise risk management programs.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and maintaining a collaborative relationship with the Chief Counsel, the Compliance Officer will serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and university leadership. This individual will establish, guide, and maintain a comprehensive compliance, ethics, and risk mitigation program that supports Purdue Global’s mission while aligning with the Purdue system’s enterprise-wide compliance framework.

The Compliance Officer will provide leadership across a complex regulatory landscape that includes federal and state higher education requirements, accreditation, educational technology governance, data privacy, accessibility, multi-state employment compliance, and enterprise risk management. The successful candidate will bring sound judgment, executive presence, and the ability to translate evolving regulatory requirements into practical institutional strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory and Statutory Compliance

  • Direct and oversee compliance strategies related to federal and state higher education regulations.
  • Provide institutional leadership regarding Title IV financial aid regulations, Title IX, the Violence Against Women Act, FERPA, and consumer protection disclosure requirements.
  • Oversee compliance with State Authorization Reciprocity Agreements and other multi-state authorization requirements affecting online education.
  • Monitor federal and state legislative and regulatory developments and lead proactive institutional responses.
  • Coordinate compliance activities involving the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights, Indiana Commission for Higher Education, state workforce agencies, and other regulatory bodies.

Enterprise Risk Management and Policy Leadership

  • Design, implement, and lead the university’s enterprise risk management practices in alignment with Purdue system frameworks.
  • Identify and assess operational, cybersecurity, financial, academic, regulatory, and reputational risks.
  • Collaborate with Purdue system Risk Management and Internal Audit teams.
  • Develop compliance dashboards, risk registers, and key risk indicators that support timely decision-making and proactive mitigation.
  • Connect risk indicators with Purdue Global quality assurance measures and strategic academic and operational initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Emerging Technology and Digital Learning Governance

  • Participate in enterprise processes that establish and maintain compliance frameworks for artificial intelligence and machine learning in academic and administrative operations.
  • Provide leadership regarding artificial intelligence ethics, educational technology governance, and responsible institutional use.
  • Champion digital accessibility requirements, including the Americans with Disabilities Act, Sections 504 and 508, and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
  • Monitor student and employee data privacy requirements under FERPA, state privacy laws, and applicable international frameworks such as the General Data Protection Regulation.
  • Partner with the Chief Information Officer and other leaders to address risks associated with remote proctoring, biometric and related data, cloud-hosted instructional tools, and emerging technologies.

Accreditation

  • Partner with the Chief Academic Officer, academic deans, and accreditation liaisons to support continued compliance with institutional and programmatic accreditation requirements.
  • Support compliance with Higher Learning Commission expectations and specialized accrediting bodies.
  • Ensure adherence to federal distance education requirements, including Regular and Substantive Interaction standards.

Audits, Investigations, and Employment Compliance

  • Direct institutional preparation and response for federal compliance audits, annual Single Audits, state agency reviews, and independent evaluations.
  • Oversee responses to reports received through the university’s anonymous whistleblower hotline.
  • Direct objective, timely, and legally sound reviews of reported noncompliance.
  • Collaborate with Human Resources on multi-state employment compliance for a distributed workforce, including requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, and Americans with Disabilities Act.

Executive Advising and Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted compliance and risk advisor to the CEO and university leadership.
  • Prepare and present executive summaries, compliance dashboards, quarterly risk registers, and recommendations to the CEO, university board, and Core Leadership Team.
  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of compliance directors and specialists.
  • Navigate sensitive academic and administrative matters with discretion, diplomacy, and sound judgment.

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in higher education administration, public policy, business administration, or a closely related field.
  • Ten years of progressively responsible leadership experience in compliance, regulatory affairs, legal services, or risk management.
  • At least five years of senior-level leadership experience within a higher education environment.
  • Significant experience interpreting and applying U.S. Department of Education regulations, including Title IV, FERPA, and Title IX.
  • Experience with multi-state authorization requirements affecting online or distance education.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing long-term operational and strategic initiatives.
  • Experience designing or coordinating enterprise risk management frameworks in collaboration with internal audit, legal, risk management, or related university functions.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, mediation, and advisory skills.
  • Ability to manage confidential matters and navigate complex academic and administrative decision-making processes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor degree.
  • Advanced knowledge of accreditation, online education, and distance learning regulatory requirements.
  • Experience with educational technology governance, artificial intelligence and machine learning compliance, data privacy, and digital accessibility standards.
  • Experience developing executive-level risk registers, compliance dashboards, and key risk indicators.
  • Compliance leadership experience within a large university system or complex online higher education institution.

About Purdue Global

Purdue Global is Purdue University’s online university for working adults. The university provides flexible, career-focused educational opportunities designed to help students develop the knowledge and skills needed to achieve their professional goals.

The Compliance Officer will have the opportunity to shape a comprehensive compliance and risk management program that supports innovation, academic quality, institutional integrity, and responsible growth across a dynamic online university.

Application Procedures

This is a remote position. The successful candidate must be able to work effectively within a highly collaborative, geographically distributed environment and may be required to travel periodically for university meetings, audits, regulatory engagements, or other institutional activities.

Application materials should include:

  • A cover letter describing the candidate’s interest in the position and relevant leadership experience
  • A current résumé or curriculum vitae
  • Contact information for professional references ( references will not be contacted without permission from the candidate)
  • Application deadline: December 10, 2026

Additional Information:

  • The anticipated annual salary for this position is $175,000. The final salary offer will be determined based on various factors, including internal equity, available budget, and relevant experience.
  • Purdue University Global will not sponsor employment authorization for this position.
  • A background check will be required for employment in this position.
  • We ask that our remote employees have access to a reliable internet connection and a dedicated, properly equipped workspace that is free of distractions.
  • Exempt (Not Eligible For Overtime) This position is generally classified as exempt unless a non-exempt classification is required by applicable state law.

Job Family

Legal and Compliance

EOE

Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university. Our goal is to recruit and retain talent from a broad pool of applicants. Purdue Global celebrates a variety of perspectives, experiences, and skills to support a success-focused environment for employees and students. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. All are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.excerpt: About the role Nucleus Financial Platforms runs its data estate on Microsoft Fabric.
jobs.description:
About the role
Nucleus Financial Platforms runs its data estate on Microsoft Fabric. The Data team brings together data from across the group's platforms and enterprise systems and turns it into a trusted, well governed foundation for the business. That foundation supports management information, financial reporting, self service analytics, our growing use of AI, and regulatory reporting.
Data Analysts connect the business, Change and Data Engineering. They make sure requirements are clearly understood and delivered, and that the data the business uses is accurate, consistent and trusted.
As a Senior Data Analyst you will own larger and less defined pieces of work end to end. You will act as the translation layer between the business, Change and the Data team, completing the up front analysis that data engineering depends on: requirements, source scoping and profiling, data definitions, conceptual and logical models, source to target mappings and non-functional requirements, so that work can be estimated accurately and built without rework. You will also build and release the more complex semantic models and reports yourself, keep the backlog moving, and raise the standard of the analysts around you.
How we work
We work in an Agile cycle alongside a Data Product Owner, with work managed through a shared backlog in Azure DevOps. Analysis comes before build: larger items are scoped, profiled, defined and specified before engineering effort is committed, so estimates are accurate and work is built once. Reports and semantic models are version controlled through Fabric Git integration and promoted through Fabric deployment pipelines across development, test and live. Every output is peer reviewed and validated before release, anything touching regulatory reporting carries an additional test and approval gate, and documentation of definitions, mappings and decisions is treated as part of the delivery rather than an afterthought. In this role you will be expected to uphold that way of working and help improve it.
Responsibilities:
  • Own requirements and specification: Act as the main point of contact between the business, Change and the Data team for your workstream, turning business requirements into build ready technical specifications, and explaining data constraints and options back in plain language.
  • Lead analysis for engineering work: Complete the up front analysis for larger items, including source profiling, mapping, model design and non-functional requirements such as refresh frequency, volumes and retention, so that engineering effort can be estimated accurately and built without rework.
  • Scope new sources: Establish what data exists in each system in scope, covering structure, volumes, refresh frequency, quality and ownership, how the system exposes its data, whether by API, scheduled file extract or direct database connection, and how it is expected to flow into OneLake and the warehouse.
  • Define and model data: Produce conceptual and logical data models, source to target mappings, business definitions and reference data, and get them agreed and signed off with system owners and the business.
  • Coordinate systems access: Identify the connections, credentials and API access a new source needs, raise the requests, and work with IT, Information Security and suppliers to get access in place, tested and evidenced.
  • Build semantic models and reports: Design, build and release Fabric semantic models, DAX measures, Power BI reports and paginated reports that stand up to scrutiny from senior stakeholders, keeping business logic in the warehouse and measures consistent.
  • Manage and burn down the backlog: Triage and size incoming work, agree priority with the Data Product Owner and stakeholders, drive items through to completion, and report throughput and burn down position to the Data Lead.
  • Data quality and assurance: Validate outputs and integrated data against source, apply team standards for definitions and reconciliation, log defects, and work with system owners to resolve discrepancies.
  • Support engineering through build: Stay close to the data engineers during build and testing, resolve questions quickly, and confirm that what is delivered matches the specification.
  • Peer review: Review specifications and outputs from other analysts for correctness, consistency with agreed definitions and downstream impact, using Fabric lineage view and impact analysis to understand what a change affects.
  • Business as usual and ad-hoc requests: Absorb day to day data requests alongside planned delivery, triaging effectively to protect delivery time.
  • Handle personal and client data responsibly: Know where outputs include personal or client data, apply sensitivity labels and row-level security where appropriate, and work within data protection obligations.
  • Mentor analysts: Support analysts and developers through specification review, peer review of outputs and knowledge sharing.
  • Document decisions and handover: Maintain documentation of models, definitions, mappings, access arrangements and decisions, so that delivered work can be picked up and supported by anyone in the team.
  • Take part in Agile ceremonies: Engaged participation in planning, backlog refinement and retrospectives, and contribute to improving how the team works.
Key Skills:
  • Advanced SQL: Strong SQL for complex analysis, data profiling, query optimisation and reconciliation across systems.
  • Requirements to specification: Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications that data engineers can build from without further analysis.
  • Data modelling: Experience producing conceptual and logical data models, source to target mappings and reference data definitions, with a solid grounding in dimensional modelling, including star schemas, fact grain and slowly changing dimensions.
  • Semantic modelling and DAX: Building semantic models, DAX measures and reports that stand up to scrutiny from senior stakeholders, with a clear view of where logic belongs between the warehouse and the model.
  • Systems and integration knowledge: An understanding of how enterprise and corporate systems expose data, for example APIs, scheduled extracts and direct database connections, and what that means for integration design.
  • Backlog management and delivery at pace: Experience owning and burning down a backlog, sizing work, prioritising with stakeholders and delivering to committed dates.
  • Stakeholder management: Confident working with Change, operations and senior stakeholders, and comfortable challenging scope where it is not deliverable.
  • Data quality and governance: Discipline around definitions, lineage and reconciliation, and awareness of data protection obligations where outputs include personal or client data.
  • Mentoring: Proven ability to guide analysts and developers and raise standards through review and knowledge sharing.
  • Agile working: Experience of working in an Agile delivery environment.
Desirable Experience:
  • Microsoft Fabric: Practical experience of the Fabric Lakehouse, Fabric Data Warehouse, OneLake, Data Pipelines, Notebooks and semantic models, including Direct Lake, Git integration and deployment pipelines. A certification such as DP-600 is welcome but not required.
  • Regulated financial services: Experience delivering data used for management, financial or regulatory reporting, and working under formal change control.
  • Platform and product domain: Wrap, SIPP, pensions or investment platform data.
  • Integration and migration projects: Experience of data analysis on systems integration, migration or platform projects, including working with third party suppliers.
  • Python: Working knowledge of Python in Fabric Notebooks for profiling and data handling.
A little about us
We are the Nucleus Group Services Limited and we help make retirement more rewarding. Here at Nucleus, people come first - whether it’s our colleagues, or the advisers and customers we support, we know that working in partnership and collaboration leads to the best outcomes. Together, we’ve shaped the platform to how it is today. We work hard, and we celebrate hard too.
Our ambition is to create a platform with a difference, putting the customer centre stage meant tearing up the rule book and starting from scratch. We’ve come a long way since then, but our mission remains just as focused. That’s why our culture, values, and social responsibility are things we keep at the top of our agenda – because we know they matter and have a big impact.
Our culture is one of the many things that sets us apart from the pack. We want to have an environment where our people feel that they can make a real difference, know they’ll be rewarded for their efforts and more importantly, enjoy themselves at work.
Inclusion and diversity at Nucleus
As with most things in life, who cares, wins. We really care about inclusion.
For us it’s not a tick box exercise; inclusion and diversity are embedded in our culture and everything we do. It’s a commercial imperative. It isn’t about being PC. It’s about being future-relevant and durable. We owe it to ourselves and the industry to ensure we are playing our part in creating a fair, balanced and transparent financial services sector.
More diversity means broader experience, a wider set of perspectives and a better collective ability to problem-solve. And it means being more representative of customer groups, which supports areas such as product development.
At Nucleus, we offer a generous blend of benefits for the things that really matter to our people, including a non-contributory pension, bonus, enhanced parental leave, paid time off for emergencies, health and wellbeing initiatives and flexible working options.

About V4C

V4C is a pure-play Databricks partner, and in under two years we have earned 850+ Databricks certifications across 325+ customers and been named Databricks' 2026 Partner of the Year (C&SI Emerging).

As a Databricks QA Engineer on our data engineering team you will own the quality gate for enterprise data platforms, working directly with customers. You will work on live enterprise data platforms alongside one of the most heavily Databricks-certified delivery teams in the market.

The Role

This is a QA role for people who understand data engineering, not general software QA pointed at a data project. You will validate Lakehouse pipelines, which means reasoning about row counts, schema drift, late-arriving data, and silent transformation errors no UI will ever surface. Our approach is automation-first: suites in Python and PySpark, running in CI, blocking promotion when they fail. You own release sign-off, which makes you the last person between a customer and bad data in production.

Responsibilities

  • Own test strategy and release sign-off on engagements, including documented test plans covering scope, risk, and coverage
  • Build and maintain automated test suites in Python and PySpark (pytest), integrated into CI pipelines
  • Validate data pipelines end to end: ingestion, Medallion layer transformations, Delta Lake tables, and ELT workflows
  • Implement data quality rules as code, including Lakeflow expectations and reusable validation frameworks
  • Run regression validation after code changes and maintain CI quality gates that block merge or promotion on failure
  • Partner with engineers to identify automation candidates and raise the coverage bar across the practice

Requirements

  • 5+ years in QA automation or test engineering, including meaningful time testing data pipelines rather than applications alone
  • A data engineering background: you can read a pipeline, reason about a transformation, and write the SQL to verify it
  • Expert-level SQL
  • Experience with Medallion architecture, Delta Lake, and ELT-based data platforms
  • Experience building automated suites that run in CI and gate deployment
  • Demonstrable hands-on experience working on Databricks or similar platforms

Preferences

  • Healthcare or life sciences experience preferred but not required
  • Existing Databricks certification(s)
  • Hands-on experience with Unity Catalog, Lakeflow pipelines, or Databricks Asset Bundles
  • Experience with Azure DevOps pipelines, or equivalent CI tooling (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
  • Familiarity with contract-based data validation standards such as ODCS
  • Experience using LLM agents or MCP-connected tooling to run validations, triage failures, or draft defect reports
  • Consulting or client-facing background

Benefits

Pay Rate: $70 – $80 per hour (1099 independent contractor).

This is a contract engagement rather than a salaried employee role. Where a rate lands within the range depends on depth of data-pipeline testing experience and automation capability. Open to contractors anywhere in the United States.

Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:

As a Creative Quality & Compliance Specialist, you’ll play an integral part in the overall quality and regulatory integrity of creative output across the Healthcare division, serving as the quality and compliance checkpoint within the creative production workflow. In this role, you’ll report directly to the Creative department and work alongside Creative Project Managers who own delivery timelines and task trafficking.

You will act as the gate through which every piece of creative passes before it reaches client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR) reviewers and again before it goes live. You'll review ads, landing pages, emails, social content, and video for MLR regulatory compliance, brand and design standards, and copy accuracy. Additionally, you’ll operate hands-on inside Veeva Vault PromoMats—managing claims, annotations, references, and submission packages—while building and refining the quality standards the creative team works against to raise the bar across the healthcare portfolio.

While your primary authority is quality and compliance, you’ll also support the creative production workflow by maintaining deliverable trackers, coordinating feedback cycles with client stakeholders, and trafficking tasks between the creative team and client POCs. As the Creative Project Manager and Account PM lead delivery management at scale, you will keep the creative lane organized and moving while ensuring nothing ships that shouldn’t.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Pre-Submission Compliance QA: Review all creative assets against MLR requirements — claims accuracy, fair balance, ISI placement, reference linking, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness rules — before they enter client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory review.
  • Post-Approval Launch QA: Final quality proof of approved assets — landing pages, ads, emails, creative — before they go live, confirming that approved content was implemented correctly and no errors were introduced in production.
  • Veeva Vault PromoMats Operations: Own the hands-on Veeva workflow — annotating assets, entering and linking claims, managing references, tracking submission status, and packaging 2253 filings.
  • Brand & Design Standards Enforcement: Review creative output for visual consistency, spec adherence, and style guide compliance across all healthcare client deliverables.
  • Copy Quality Review: Review all copy for grammar, tone, messaging accuracy, and alignment with approved claims and client brand voice.
  • QA Process Documentation & Refinement: Build, maintain, and continuously improve the quality and compliance standards, checklists, and review processes the creative team follows.
  • Creative Workflow Coordination: Support creative production operations alongside the Creative Project Manager and Account PM — maintaining Asana boards and deliverable trackers, communicating timelines and managing feedback cycles with client stakeholders, trafficking tasks between the creative team and client POCs, coordinating with cross-channel PMs on shared deliverables, and organizing client-provided assets within Power Digital’s file structure.
  • Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes.
  • Utilize and leverage Power Digital’s Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department.
  • Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

  • 4+ years in healthcare or pharmaceutical creative production, agency or in-house, with direct exposure to MLR review workflows
  • Demonstrated understanding of FDA OPDP guidance and 21 CFR 202, including fair balance, ISI placement, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness content rules, and 2253 filing requirements
  • Veeva Vault PromoMats experience (annotating, claims management, submission tracking) highly preferred
  • Strong eye for brand consistency, design quality, and copy accuracy across digital formats (paid social, display, landing pages, email)
  • Process-oriented with the ability to document, maintain, and improve QA standards without external direction
  • Comfortable reviewing and providing clear, actionable feedback on creative work from designers, copywriters, and freelancers
  • Proficiency with Asana or comparable project management platforms
  • Experience working alongside project management teams in a fast-paced agency environment
  • Bonus: Veeva PromoMats certification, experience with modular content strategies, or prior work across both pharma-regulated and non-regulated healthcare clients

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • First-pass approval rate: 80%+ of assets cleared by client M/L/R reviewers on first submission
  • QA turnaround time: internal reviews completed within defined SLA (e.g. 24–48 hours)
  • Pre-launch error rate: <2% of launched assets requiring post-launch correction
  • 100% accuracy on 2253 filings and regulatory submission packaging
  • Documented QA standards maintained and current across all supported accounts

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • Establish the pre-submission and pre-launch QA checkpoints as defined, repeatable stages in the creative workflow.
  • Own the Veeva PromoMats workflow for assigned accounts — claims, annotations, references, and submissions operating cleanly from day one.
  • Build and maintain the QA standards documentation (checklists, compliance reference guides, brand review criteria) the creative team works against.
  • Develop a working rhythm with Creative Project Managers so that QA is a checkpoint in the pipeline, not a bottleneck.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Base salary + commission opportunities
  • Prepaid Medicine Plan
  • 15 paid vacation days (PTO) per year
  • Up to 4 hours per quarter for paid Volunteer Time Off (VTO) towards philanthropic endeavors
  • Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
  • A one time 400.000 COP Work From Home (WFH) stipend automatically added to your first paycheck
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • 17 observed Colombian national holidays + 2 mental health recharge days per year
  • Legal benefits like Prima, Cesantias
  • Paid Social Security
  • Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
  • Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
  • Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
  • Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

COMPANY PROFILE

CodeAI is an education innovation nonprofit dedicated to the vision that every student in every school has the opportunity to learn about artificial intelligence (AI) and computer science (CS) as part of their core K-12 education. We increase participation in AI+CS education by reaching students of all backgrounds where they are — at their skill level, in their schools, and in ways that inspire them to keep learning, with a focus on increasing participation by young women and students from other underrepresented groups. The leading provider of K-12 AI+CS education curriculum across the globe, CodeAI also organizes the annual Hour of AI campaign, building on the legacy of the Hour of Code, which has engaged more than 15% of all students in the world!

A unifying approach in a divided world

CodeAI's global role in the K-12 computer science movement is only possible because we use a unifying approach across diverse and often divided stakeholders. At a time of increasing polarization, the idea of increasing opportunity for students unites people from across the political spectrum. CodeAI's team members, students, teachers, and supporters have diverse and diverging view points, and they are all welcome in our mission. Read more.

JOB SUMMARY

The Director of Development is a key contributor on CodeAI’s Revenue and Development team, responsible for stewarding and growing our largest existing donor relationships across individuals, foundations, and corporate partners. This role directly manages a personal portfolio of high-value donors. The Director of Development will collaborate closely with executive leadership, program, and product teams to craft tailored partnership strategies that advance both donor goals and CodeAI’s mission. This position is essential to sustaining our impact and ensuring long-term revenue predictability.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

In this role you will:

  • Serve as the relationship owner for a portfolio of CodeAI’s most significant existing donors, including top foundations, Fortune 500 companies, and high-net-worth individuals
  • Develop and execute customized renewal and upsell strategies for each account, focusing on multi-year and unrestricted commitments
  • Mentor a high-performing team of two fundraisers responsible for donor renewals across corporate and individual segments
  • Partner with internal teams (Programs, Marketing, Product, Finance) to craft compelling impact reports, renewal proposals, and donor engagement materials
  • Serve as a primary development liaison for internal executive and program leadership when coordinating on complex or multi-stakeholder renewals
  • Collaborate with CodeAI’s leadership team to shape the overall donor stewardship strategy and ensure consistent, high-quality engagement
  • Monitor portfolio health and team performance using Salesforce and other tools to track renewals, revenue forecasts, and donor activity
  • Identify and resolve potential churn risks early through proactive outreach and value reinforcement
  • Represent CodeAI at donor meetings, conferences, and high-level events to strengthen relationships and increase visibility
  • Ensure high standards of operational excellence, data integrity, and donor experience throughout the renewal process
  • Contribute to long-term planning and strategic growth of the fundraising function, including ideas for segmentation, tiering, and team structure
  • Partner with the SVP of Revenue, Chief Growth Officer, and President as needed for top-tier donor engagement and executive sponsorship strategy

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

We seek candidates who have:

  • 8+ years of experience in fundraising, strategic partnerships, or enterprise sales, with a focus on renewals and account growth
  • Proven success managing high-value donor or customer relationships ($500K+ annual value), preferably in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization
  • Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and negotiation skills with executive-level audiences
  • Deep understanding of donor stewardship best practices and a strong customer success mindset
  • Skilled in managing complex, multi-stakeholder accounts and cross-functional collaboration
  • Strong data orientation with experience using Salesforce or similar CRMs to manage portfolios and forecast revenue
  • Highly organized with excellent project management and follow-through skills
  • Mission-driven, intellectually curious, and energized by systems change and educational equity
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree a plus

In addition, candidates must:

  • Be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident
  • Work within the continental United States
  • Pass a pre-employment background check
  • Be willing to travel a minimum of two times per year for team events

OUR CULTURAL PRINCIPLES

The way we work matters as much as the work itself. Before you apply, we invite you to take a look at our cultural principles. They reflect who we are, how we show up for each other, and what we look for in the people who join us.

OUR APPROACH TO AI IN HIRING

At CodeAI, we use AI thoughtfully and responsibly to support human-centered hiring. AI may help with administrative tasks, but every hiring decision is made by real people on our team. We welcome candidates to use AI appropriately in their job search while upholding our values of honesty and integrity throughout the process.

Read our full AI Use Policy in Hiring here.

WHAT IS THE INTERVIEW PROCESS LIKE?

Step 1: Informational Interview - learn more about the role and share your experience (30 minutes)
Step 2: Interviews with members of the CodeAI team (~ 2 hours)

Step 3: Homework (~3 hours)

Step 4: Panel Interview (1 hour)

Step 5: Final Interview (1 hour)

Step 6: Reference Checks

All interviews are currently being conducted virtually via Google Meet

TO APPLY

Our team will review all applications on an ongoing basis and if we believe your qualifications would make a great fit, we'll contact you to schedule an informational interview.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS PACKAGE

The expected salary range for this position is $124,200 - $138,000. Most offers are on the lower end of the salary range and are at the company’s sole discretion based on the final candidate’s experience. This allows us to provide a fair and equitable approach to compensation when setting pay and maintaining internal pay equity.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees that includes:

  • Technology subsidy consistent with our Bring Your Own Device environment
  • Flexible, engaging, and remote working environment
  • Paid time off: 5 weeks total, comprised of 3 weeks vacation annually, plus a 2-week winter break office closure (including Christmas and New Year's), and sick leave
  • Medical, dental and vision premiums paid at 100% for FT positions and their dependents
  • Option to participate in 403b retirement plan
  • The opportunity to help students learn better and change the face of computer science

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

About Us:

We are a team of marketing strategists, digital innovators, life science leaders, and other professionals who are driving growth, pushing the envelope, and going above and beyond on behalf of our clients every day.

PharmaForceIQ is a real-time customer engagement platform built specifically for life sciences. We empower leaders across functions and brands with a faster, more effective way to engage healthcare professionals and patients. By streamlining real-time optichannel execution, leveraging AI, and focusing on measurable impact, we are driving a paradigm shift from sluggish, siloed customer engagement efforts to agile, data-driven strategies that deliver unmatched efficiency and tangible results.

Position Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Product Engineer with a minimum of 3-6 years of experience in pharma commercial or media SaaS. The ideal candidate will be responsible for Owning the UI product portfolio, Designing and prototype UI/UX with AI among other tasks . This role requires you to turn the roadmap into working screens, prototype them with AI tools, test them with our internal experts, and work hands-on with our front-end engineers until they ship.Product Engineer will report to the Director of Product or Similar.

Key Responsibilities:

Own the UI product portfolio

  • Own the roadmap for our customer-facing UI: the platform home, setup screens, journey and trigger builders, planning workspace and reporting views.
  • Turn business goals and customer needs into clear epics, user stories and acceptance criteria that engineers can build without guessing.
  • Prioritize the backlog against delivery capacity, customer commitments and the wider product roadmap.

Design and prototype UI/UX with AI

  • Design flows and screens, and build working prototypes using AI tools (for example Claude, Cursor, v0, Lovable or Figma AI) on our demo environment.
  • Test prototypes with internal subject-matter experts in customer engagement, data science and commercial teams, and iterate before engineering starts.
  • Hand off prototypes that are ready to build: agreed behaviour, edge cases, data needs and design consistency with the rest of the product.

Work hands-on with front-end engineers

  • Act as product owner for the front-end team: bring stories that are ready to build into each sprint, within the cadence and release train the TPM runs.
  • Answer product questions during the sprint, review work in progress and accept it against the definition of done.
  • Work closely with backend, data science and QA so UI work is not blocked by missing APIs or data.

Join customer conversations (optional)

  • If you are able and interested, join customer calls to demo your screens and gather feedback, then bring it back into the roadmap. This is an opportunity, not a regular part of the role.

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years in the pharmaceutical industry, working on commercial or media-related SaaS products (for example CRM, omnichannel engagement, HCP targeting, next-best-action, marketing analytics or programmatic media).
  • A working understanding of pharma commercial operations: brand teams, field force, HCP segmentation and targeting, multichannel campaigns and compliance constraints.
  • Experience as a product manager, product owner or technical product manager for a web application, owning a roadmap and backlog.
  • Solid understanding of UI/UX programming and technology: modern front-end frameworks (React or similar), component libraries, APIs, and what makes a screen easy or hard to build.
  • Hands-on UX design skills: user flows, wireframes, interactive prototypes, and usability testing with real users.
  • Day-to-day Scrum experience with engineering teams, including writing stories with clear acceptance criteria; comfortable in Jira.
  • Clear written and spoken English, and the confidence to present to customers and senior stakeholders.

Nice to have

  • Experience at a pharma commercial technology, data or consulting firm.
  • Vibe-coding experience: shipping working prototypes or small apps mostly through AI coding tools, with a portfolio or GitHub you can show us.
  • Experience designing AI-assisted features, such as AI drafts that users review and approve.
  • Familiarity with pharma CRM platforms or the digital media vendors used in pharma.
  • Exposure to data products built on Databricks, Snowflake or similar platforms.
  • Experience working in the health-tech industry is preferred.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple projects simultaneously.

What success looks like

30 days

You know the product, the UI team and the roadmap, and own the front-end backlog.

90 days

At least one new screen has gone from AI prototype through SME testing to production. UI stories are ready before every sprint, and engineers rarely wait on product decisions.

6 months

Each roadmap step ships its UI on schedule; customers and internal teams give feedback through you, and it shows up in the roadmap.

12 months

You are the go-to owner for the UI portfolio, trusted by engineers, internal experts and customers alike.

Why Join Us?

  • Enjoy the flexibility of a fully remote work environment.
  • Competitive base salary (2,000,000 INR - 3,000,000 INR). Actual base pay will depend on varying circumstances, including the position, location, individual qualifications, market finances, and other operational business needs.

jobs.description:
BBCS Facilitator (Freelance / Independent Contractor)

Berlitz Business Communication Skills (BBCS)

Engagement type: Freelance, project-based independent contractor

Delivery: Virtual and/or in person, depending on the program

About the opportunity

Berlitz is building a network of independent professionals to deliver Berlitz Business Communication Skills (BBCS) programs to corporate, organizational and government clients. Participants range from individual contributors to managers and senior executives, including C-suite audiences.

As a freelance BBCS Facilitator, you bring your own professional expertise in business communication, facilitation and coaching to help participants communicate with greater clarity, confidence and impact. Engagements are offered program by program, and you choose which ones to accept based on your availability and interests.

BBCS is not language instruction. Language programs build language proficiency. BBCS develops business communication performance: how participants structure messages, respond to audiences, influence others and achieve professional objectives. Language feedback may be part of a session when it supports those objectives.

Scope of services

For each engagement you accept, services typically include:

  • Session preparation. Reviewing the client's program objectives, participant needs and business context, and preparing your approach for individual or group sessions.
  • Delivering practical sessions on workplace communication topics using case studies, simulations, role plays and realistic business scenarios.
  • Participant coaching. Providing specific, actionable feedback on clarity, structure, tone, professionalism, confidence and overall effectiveness.
  • Business relevance. Connecting program content to participants' industries, roles and workplace challenges while meeting the program's agreed learning objectives.
  • Progress reporting. Providing participant progress reports and recommendations at the points agreed for the engagement.

You determine your own facilitation methods, session approach and preparation process within the agreed program objectives and deliverables.

Program areas

BBCS programs cover one or more of the following areas. Engagements are matched to your areas of expertise.

  • Professional email and correspondence
  • Business writing and document development
  • Meeting participation and leadership
  • Presentations and executive speaking
  • Negotiation and persuasion
  • Workplace professionalism and etiquette
  • Cross-functional communication and collaboration
  • Professional relationship-building in diverse environments

Deliverables and quality standards

Each engagement is defined by agreed deliverables. Clients and Berlitz look for:

  • Sessions that are focused, engaging and aligned with the program objectives
  • Specific, useful feedback that helps participants improve

jobs.description:
Chief Revenue & Partnerships Officer | Pathfinder International

Remote based in the United States

Organizational Overview

For nearly 70 years, Pathfinder has worked alongside women and girls in more than 100 countries, ensuring they have access to critical services and resources.

Pathfinder’s women-driven, community-centered solutions advance the health, leadership, and resilience of women and girls—creating opportunities for them to thrive. Pathfinder places the experiences and voices of women and girls at the heart of its solutions, unlocking their leadership and innovation to transform the systems holding them back and build a better future for all.

Approach

Pathfinder works alongside women to reduce systemic barriers and unlock innovation so they can drive a better future for society and the environment. By co-designing solutions at the intersections of health, climate resilience, and leadership with women and their communities, the organization ensures a context-sensitive approach grounded in lived realities.

To address complex challenges, Pathfinder adopts an intersectional lens to drive meaningful change. Overcoming barriers requires a multisectoral approach, one that is interconnected with economics, education, and governance. The organization’s approach brings together stakeholders across sectors, leveraging our power to dig deeply into interconnected systems and build sustainable, scalable solutions.

Role Summary & Context for Recruitment

The Chief Revenue & Partnerships Officer (CRPO) is responsible, in partnership with the President and CEO, for building and leading an integrated revenue strategy that diversifies Pathfinder’s funding. A primary value add of this role will be driving higher unrestricted funding through philanthropic development and innovative financing to unlock new capital streams that enhance financial sustainability and resilience. Reporting to President and CEO Dr. Tabinda Sarosh, the CRPO will serve as her strategic partner in revenue generation and will work closely with the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Programs and Impact Officer, the Vice President of Strategic Engagement and Innovation, Country Directors, and the Board of Directors, led by Collin Mothupi. The CRPO will directly lead three areas: the Individual Giving Unit, including the Director of Major and Leadership Gifts; Pathfinder's emerging impact and capital investment work; and corporate partnerships. The Business Development team under the Chief Programs and Impact Officer leads proposal-based fundraising from foundations, governments, and other institutional donors.

Pathfinder conducts this search at a defining point in its nearly 70-year history. For decades, U.S. government funding underwrote much of the organization’s work, and the end of USAID support in 2025 brought that era to a close. Pathfinder had anticipated a shift in the donor landscape and was already well into a transition to a country-led model, moving leadership and support functions closer to the communities it serves. Through difficult decisions made quickly, its leadership has positioned the organization to weather this period and to set its own course. Pathfinder narrowed its focus to deliver deeper impact in fewer places and is building a revenue model that matches its mission: one grounded in local leadership and self-reliance.

The CRPO’s charge is to build that model. Pathfinder raises funds today through institutional grants and through an Individual Giving Unit that stewards a loyal base of U.S. donors, many of whom provide unrestricted support. The organization is also developing new sources of revenue, including impact investment, blended finance, and social enterprises incubated within Pathfinder that can generate earned income. The CRPO will define a clear revenue and financial strategy that sets out what share of revenue each stream should provide, what investment each requires, and how progress will be measured. The CRPO will select and sequence the opportunities of highest potential among many and will grow individual giving from mid-level through major gifts. Over time, the CRPO is expected to integrate traditional and new approaches into a unified global revenue function and to position Pathfinder as a leader in innovative development financing.

Candidate Profile

Pathfinder will consider a broad range of backgrounds and does not expect any one candidate to bring expertise in every revenue channel. It seeks a leader with demonstrated success in both philanthropy and investment or enterprise finance, the judgment to set priorities across channels, and the ability to learn quickly where experience is lighter. The ideal candidate will align with the following qualifications:

Minimum Education and Work Experience

  • Significant senior progressive leadership experience in revenue generation, business development, strategic partnerships, philanthropy, impact investing, venture philanthropy, corporate engagement, investment management, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated success in securing and growing diversified revenue streams, including a combination of philanthropic funding, corporate partnerships, strategic alliances, impact investment, blended finance, social enterprise models, or other innovative financing mechanisms.
  • Proven experience engaging and influencing senior executives, investors, philanthropists, foundations, corporate leaders, development finance institutions, and other strategic stakeholders.
  • Strong track record of identifying, developing, and executing growth opportunities that generate both social impact and sustainable revenue.
  • Experience designing and implementing revenue diversification strategies within complex, multi-country, global, or mission-driven organizations.
  • Demonstrated commercial acumen, including the ability to evaluate market opportunities, business models, partnership structures, investment propositions, and financial sustainability.
  • Experience leading high-performing, geographically dispersed teams and building a culture of innovation, accountability, and results.
  • Exceptional relationship-building, negotiation, and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility across the private, philanthropic, public, and nonprofit sectors.
  • Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, including the ability to translate organizational priorities into executable revenue growth strategies.
  • Degree in business administration, finance, international development, economics, commercial strategy, public policy, global health or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Education and Work Experience

  • Experience working across both the private and social impact sectors.
  • Familiarity with global health, international development, women’s economic empowerment, climate, education, or other mission-driven sectors.
  • Experience with impact investing, blended finance structures, public-private partnerships, venture philanthropy, or innovative financing mechanisms.
  • Prior experience serving in a chief revenue officer, chief growth officer, chief partnerships officer, investment director, corporate development, or similar executive leadership role.

Competencies/Attributes

  • Strategic and systems thinking: Able to translate vision into actionable business development plans and to prioritize and sequence competing opportunities.
  • Executive leadership and team building: Able to inspire and unify cross-functional global teams around common goals.
  • Partnership with leadership: Confidence to set and drive a revenue agenda while keeping the CEO and Executive Leadership Team closely informed; committed to the success of the CEO and the organization.
  • Relationship management and influence: Proven ability to influence others at all levels in the organization through diplomacy and proven oral and written communication skills. Proven ability to develop and maintain donor relations.
  • Financial acumen and negotiation: Demonstrates strong financial insight and the ability to analyze revenue drivers, budgets, and business performance while effectively negotiating partnerships, contracts, and funding opportunities to achieve organizational goals and maximize sustainable revenue growth.
  • Innovation and adaptability: Thrives in evolving environments, balancing strategic priorities with on-the-ground realities.
  • Results orientation and accountability: Committed to achieving measurable outcomes within timelines and budgets.
  • Change leadership: Able to guide an organization through significant transitions or transformations by inspiring and empowering people to embrace and adapt to new directions.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset: Ability to champion innovation, opportunity recognition, proactive problem-solving and value creation. Brings a growth mindset and the drive to take new ventures from concept to revenue.
  • Integrity and accountability: Upholds the highest ethical standards, ensuring transparency and responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
  • Cultural competency: Demonstrates sensitivity and respect for diverse cultural contexts, and welcomes working with colleagues, partners, and donors across many cultures and languages.
  • Organization, planning, and multi-tasking: Has in-depth demonstrated organizational and planning skills, project planning, and management skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality in work-related matters.
  • Languages: Advanced writing and speaking skills in English; proficiency in additional languages spoken in Pathfinder’s regions is a plus.
  • Foundational knowledge of women’s health and agency principles, practices, and services, including program strategies and indicators.
  • Travel: ability to travel as needed for the role.

Equal Employment Opportunity Employer Statement

Pathfinder International provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Safeguarding and Protection Statement

Pathfinder is committed to the safeguarding and protection of the people we serve and our staff. We have zero tolerance for any type of behavior that inflicts harm on children, young people, adults, our staff, and partners including sexual abuse, harassment, bullying, and exploitation. We do everything possible to ensure that we recruit only those who are suitable to work with for us and expect that everyone we hire will abide by our safeguarding and related policies and will report any suspected or known violations. This job is subject to a range of vetting checks as legally permitted in the country where they are being hired. Senior Product Engineer (Node), LeadConduit

Company Overview

ActiveProspect is on a mission to make consent-based marketing the best channel for online customer acquisition. We provide marketers the products they need to acquire qualified customers at scale. Our platform is trusted by thousands of companies engaged in direct-to-consumer marketing, helping them save wasted spend, comply with ever-changing regulations, and manage a constantly evolving partner landscape.

Our flagship product, TrustedForm, is used to certify over 1 billion opt-in digital customer leads every year and is the gold standard for documenting prior express written consent for TCPA compliance. LeadConduit, our real-time lead processing and routing platform, connects lead sellers and buyers and checks consent, data quality, and delivery rules on every lead.

Job Summary

You own customer and business outcomes, not tickets. You work like a forward-deployed engineer: you belong to the LeadConduit team, and you contribute to projects, initiatives, and pods where the problem is, deliver your work across the full stack (Vue/Nuxt and React/Next.js on the frontend, Node.js and TypeScript services on AWS), and improve processes for delivery in future projects. The technical bar is high, but coding ability is only the starting point. What sets this role apart is judgment: knowing the smallest thing worth shipping, when to drop your own idea, and when AI output is good enough versus when to override it. On LeadConduit, that work splits evenly between two areas: keeping today's platform fast and reliable for the customers who run their business on it, and building the next-generation platform, including a new real-time engine for ping/post, call tracking, and buyer optimization.

You'll move between the LeadConduit team and the initiatives you deploy into, shipping early, talking to customers, and deciding fast.

Responsibilities

  • Own outcomes end-to-end, wherever you're assigned. Frame the problem, design it, ship it, own the metric. Distill to the cheapest version that works. Prototype in days.
  • Work across today's LeadConduit and the next-generation platform. Improve the current product (flows, integrations, reporting) and help build the new real-time engine (field mapping, ping/post, call tracking, buyer optimization).
  • Stay close to customers. Shadow sales and support, talk with lead buyers and sellers, join advisory conversations, and let customer reality drive technical decisions. Propose what to build, defer, and drop.
  • Own your domain and share it. Its interfaces, reliability, performance, and security, including on-call for the systems you own. Consent, TCPA compliance, and PII handling are central to customer trust. Bring patterns, tooling, and hard-won context back to the wider org rather than hoarding them.
  • Build and scale both the product surface and the platform beneath it. Ship responsive, accessible interfaces with a strong UI/UX eye (Vue/Nuxt today, React/Next.js for the new platform), back them with Node.js and TypeScript services and APIs, and keep the real-time, multi-tenant lead and call processing engine reliable and fast as volume grows.
  • Architect AI-driven leverage. Build AI-assisted workflows that hold up, evolve the team's practices as tooling changes (Cursor, Claude Code, and whatever comes next), and look for product wins AI unlocks (smarter routing, anomaly detection on lead flow, AI-built integrations, and more).
  • Make every team you work with stronger. Mentor on judgment and product sense, not just syntax. Write decision memos and ADRs. Enable Product and Design to self-serve.

Qualifications and Skills

  • A track record of shipping something end-to-end that you cared about and owning the outcome, not just the code.
  • Product judgment: pushing back on a bad spec, proposing the cheapest experiment, descoping, and collaborating with Product to suggest solutions rather than waiting for a fully specified ticket.
  • Comfort embedding with unfamiliar teams and codebases, getting productive fast, and leaving them better than you found them.
  • Deep full-stack expertise: React/Next.js and Vue/Nuxt (component lifecycle, state management, rendering optimization), JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern CSS on the frontend; Node.js and TypeScript services, RESTful APIs, and low-latency, high-volume asynchronous data handling on the backend.
  • Cloud and real-time systems depth: AWS core services (Lambda, EC2, S3, DynamoDB, API Gateway) and event-driven, queue-based processing (SQS, SNS, Kafka, or similar) to deliver multi-tenant, real-time products reliably at scale.
  • A strong UI/UX eye: you turn wireframes, mockups, and ambiguous requirements into intuitive, accessible, user-centric journeys.
  • Strong systems design judgment in ambiguous contexts, and a security mindset aligned with sensitive consumer data and compliance.
  • Lead generation or performance marketing experience is a strong plus: ping/post, lead routing and distribution, call tracking, or TCPA and consent rules.
  • Fluency building your own AI-assisted workflows and reading AI output critically. Daily use of AI-native tools (Cursor, Claude Code) and precise prompting across OpenAI and Claude models, with the judgment to know when to trust output, how to review it for hidden bugs and security issues, and when to override it.
  • Clear written and verbal communication. Mentorship experience. 5-10% travel.

How It Works

You'll report to an Engineering Manager who owns several teams and stays out of their daily flow. As you embed, you'll often act as the player-coach Tech Lead, owning technical direction while the EM owns delivery health and stakeholder alignment across the group.

Success looks like movement in a user or business metric your team owns, high-value work deliberately not built, decisions made fast, and teams that move faster after you've worked with them, not just while you're there.

Engineering Manager

Position Summary

The Statistical Programming Summer Internship provides a master’s-level student with the opportunity to apply programming, data science, automation, and emerging technologies to real-world challenges in clinical development.
The intern will work alongside experienced statistical programmers and cross-functional partners on a defined project focused on improving the efficiency, quality, or scalability of clinical data and statistical programming processes. Depending on project assignment, the work may involve clinical trial data and metadata, CDISC standards, SAS or R programming, Python-based automation, generative AI, validation and testing, or development of reusable programming solutions. jobs.title: VP, Mozilla Studio
jobs.excerpt: Mozilla Foundationis a non-profit building a better technology future — powered by people, open by design, fueled by imagination.
jobs.description:
Mozilla Foundationis a non-profit building a better technology future — powered by people, open by design, fueled by imagination.

We deliver people-first alternatives to today’s extractive systems. We build side by side with developers, innovators and advocates, united in the belief that a better technology future is not only possible — it’s ours to create!

Team

One of the ways we are deepening our commitment to building side by side with innovators is Mozilla Studio: where we find promising builders and ideas, select the ones worth backing, and help them become tools and technology actually used by people and institutions. It is where the critical step from promising idea to workable, sustainable tool happens.

Good public-interest technology often fails between prototype and first user, because commercial capital arrives on terms at odds with the mission, and grant capital rarely comes with the help a team needs on sustainment, supply, and operational excellence. Mozilla Studio, building on the work of our Incubator, helps to close that gap. It backs efforts early, gives teams what they need, and connects them to the deployers, buyers, and follow-on funders who help make these alternatives true defaults. Our goal is technology that lasts beyond our funding.

This newly created role of VP, Mozilla Studio will hold the responsibility of building and running the Studio. You'll start with an active portfolio, including our current AI initiatives, and keep that work moving without disruption while you set the Studio's direction.

This role reports directly to the CEO and partners closely with the Operations Team to steward the Studio's legal, compliance, financial, and logistical obligations, keeping handoffs clear so the Studio runs smoothly across the Foundation.

This is a remote role open to candidates based in Canada, Germany, the UK, or the US.

Job responsibilities

As the VP, Mozilla Studio, you will…

  • Take the helm of the Studio’s active portfolio, including our current AI initiatives. You’ll keep it moving while you build trusted relationships with the CEO, teams across the Foundation, and builders.
  • Assess each active bet rigorously to understand who it serves, what early signals it’s showing, and what it will take to reach its next stage.
  • Set the Studio's direction and criteria for what it backs, extends, stops, or declines, and decide how much support each team gets within our agreed investment timelines. Every decision ties back to technology people can use, held by teams that can stand on their own.
  • Hold every bet to a clear standard: a deployer or user named up front, with progress measured in adoption and impact rather than activity.
  • Pressure-test every commitment before capital moves to understand whether we can make a meaningful difference, and whether our risk capital can unblock something uniquely within our reach.
  • Balance early signals across the portfolio against bigger conviction bets. Make disciplined stop decisions at the right moments and document the rationale behind each.
  • Guide each team to a durable structure (a company, nonprofit, cooperative, mission entity, or commons project) with a working sustaining model and at least one named funder beyond us.
  • Build and lead a high-performing Studio team and a bench of talent calibrated to support each team's stage and timeline.
  • Set up clear and dependable handoffs with the Investment Committee and other Foundation teams, so the Studio works seamlessly across the organization and investment cycle.
  • Translate portfolio evidence into clear signals for leadership, the Board and our funders, with candor about what we expected, what happened, and where we fell short.
  • Make the Studio a place serious engineers and founders want to be, and a trusted source of vetted opportunities for deployers and co-funders.

Your Professional Profile

  • Proven track record building or leading a studio, incubator, lab, accelerator or early-stage founder program at a senior level, working hands-on with the teams you backed
  • Technical lens to engage engineers, open source and internet infrastructure, and can rigorously test the claims teams make
  • Deep, active network of deployers, buyers, co-funders and builders across sectors and regions, with the discernment to know which ideas merit their attention
  • Fluency with capital classes. Knowledge across grants, recoverable grants, PRI, and beyond
  • Experience with at least one model beyond venture equity, such as cooperatives or public-benefit companies
  • Comfort in making the hard calls; stopping bets and saying no
  • Experience building and leading high-performing teams, and drawing in borrowed talent such as residents and advisors
  • Demonstrated commitment to Mozilla Foundation's mission and to an open, trustworthy internet
  • Flexibility to work across time zones and occasionally outside standard hours

We Are Excited To See Any Additional Experience With:

  • Nonprofit governance and Board reporting
  • Fundraising and building funder relationships
  • Depth in one or more of Mozilla Foundation's focus areas
  • Helping teams get their technology adopted by public institutions or large organizations

How We Work

A few things that are true about how we work at Mozilla Foundation. Here's a summary along with our expectation of how these should show up in this role:

  • Move toward the hard thing. Stopping a bet, or turning down a builder you like, is part of this job. Name it early, explain your reasoning to the team directly, and raise concerns in the room rather than after it.
  • Stay curious and current. Keep close to what's moving in open source, internet infrastructure and the communities our tools are meant to serve. Bring what you learn back, and test your own conviction as hard as you test a team's claims.
  • Work in the open. Document why we backed, extended or stopped each bet so leadership, the Board and funders can follow the reasoning. Share portfolio progress while it's still in progress, not only once it's polished.
  • Focus and finish. A lean Studio can't back everything. Be clear about which bets get support and why, then see each one through to a sustainable form or a well-made stop.
  • Flex with purpose. A cooperative at month four needs something different from a commons project at year two. Adjust your support as teams and context change, without drifting from the mission or the timelines agreed on.
  • Lead with care. Hold builders to high standards while remembering they're people taking real risks. Talk directly with whoever can fix a problem, and keep enough lightness in the room that people can be human.

Salary and Benefits Information

Mozilla Foundation is dedicated to fair and equitable compensation for our staff. We aim to pay a competitive and market-based salary based on the responsibilities and requirements of the role. We do not ask for, or take into account, salary histories in our offer process.

The starting salary ranges for this role are listed below.

  • Germany: €222,088.00 – €249,848.22
  • UK: £195,534.00 – £219,975.06
  • Canada: $383,400.00 – $431,323.65
  • US: $284,000 – $319,499

We also offer the following benefits:

  • Private Medical Insurance
  • Extended Sick Leave
  • Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Retirement Plan contributions
  • Paid Time Off: 20 days annual leave + sick days and your birthday
  • Company Holidays + EOY Shutdown
  • Wellness budget
  • Professional Development budget
  • Top up program for Pregnancy and Parental leaves

Benefits are subject to change at any time at the discretion of Mozilla Foundation.

Mozilla Foundation Hiring Practices

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation at .

At GreenSlate, we build powerful, highly configurable software that powers some of the most complex productions in the entertainment industry. As a Digital Implementation Specialist II, you’ll spend most of your time executing continuous, high-volume project setups and configuring our platform to meet each production’s unique requirements. This role is for someone who loves working inside sophisticated software, mastering its full range of customization options, and delivering precise, accurate setups at scale. If you’re energized by technical problem-solving and the satisfaction of a perfectly configured project, this role is for you.

This role is remote within the United States and must be located in the Pacific timezone to be considered.

WHO WE ARE

GreenSlate is the fastest-growing provider of technology and business solutions for media productions. We provide the most advanced technology for production accounting and entertainment payroll. Our innovative cloud-based platform is evolving the entertainment industry’s back-office by replacing inefficient paper-based processes with digital solutions. The studios, film franchises, independent producers, and content creators we serve benefit from greater efficiencies, better access to data, and cost savings, and they minimize their impact on the environment. H2O.ai is on a mission to democratize AI for Good.   • Be part of a world-class team

Senior Power Systems Engineer – EMT

Who We Are

The energy transition is vital to our future, and here at PSC, we are compelled to make a difference. We are specialist consultants to the energy industry, an independent firm with global operations. Our teams have been tackling the thorniest problems for some of the most prominent industry players for 30 years.
