jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Crystalia Glass LLC is a U.S.-based manufacturer and provider of premium glass solutions, specializing in custom glass partitions for residential, commercial, and institutional projects. We operate a full-cycle model — from design and manufacturing to sales, delivery, and installation.

We are strengthening our commercial function and looking for a CRM & Sales Operations Manager to own the CRM, the sales process and data quality across the full funnel, from first contact to order handover. This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role with no direct reports.

Employment Type:

  • Full-time 8.30 am - 5 pm, NY (EST zone).
  • Remote work.
  • B2B contract (sole proprietorship status or corporate entity).

Key responsibilities:

CRM setup and process design

  • Personally configure CRM fields, stages, reports and automation; scope complex changes and integrations for developers and test them before release.
  • Define rules for each stage: goal, entry and exit criteria, required data and next steps.
  • Set ownership at each stage and at handover, and agree SLAs for response time and escalation.

Process control and data quality

  • Audit deals to check that CRM stages and next steps match actual client communication.
  • Monitor overdue tasks, stalled deals, missing next steps and missing loss reasons.
  • Keep CRM data accurate and resolve recurring issues with team leads.

Training

  • Write short CRM instructions and train sales reps and team leads to manage deals correctly, including after every change.

Reporting and analytics

  • Build funnel reports and dashboards: conversion by stage, stage duration, loss reasons and SLA adherence.
  • Measure the impact of process changes and share data with sales leadership and the Sales Effectiveness Manager.

Automation and AI

  • Use AI to analyze CRM data and prepare next actions for reps, with human review before anything reaches a client.
  • Build AI workflows for the sales team and maintain AI agents and bots connected to the CRM.

Requirements

The core of this role is hands-on CRM administration and sales process design.

  • 5+ years of experience in CRM administration, sales operations or revenue operations, including owning the CRM and sales processes, not only supporting them.
  • Hands-on CRM setup (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar): fields, stages and permissions.
  • Hands-on experience bringing AI into a sales team’s daily work, from building to measuring results.
  • Understanding of the full sales cycle, from first contact to order handover.
  • Experience designing deal stages, handover rules and SLAs.
  • Experience automating deal workflows and writing requirements for integrations.
  • Experience fixing CRM data issues and building sales reports personally.
  • Strong analytical skills and careful conclusions from data.
  • Experience training sales reps to work correctly in the CRM.
  • Experience driving change through team leads without direct authority; strong team player.
  • Fluent English (C1/C2)

Nice to have

  • Setting up or migrating a CRM from scratch.
  • Experience with a complex physical product with a long sales cycle.

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses.
  • Full ownership of the CRM and sales operations in a fast-growing U.S. company, with the freedom to build them the right way.
  • Direct influence on how the sales process runs, with data that leadership relies on.
  • Hands-on work with automation and AI in real sales processes.
  • Joining a highly professional and dynamic team.
  • Exciting experience working with prestigious clients in the US market.

jobs.excerpt: DescriptionThe Site Contracts & Budget Manager provides operational leadership for site contracting and budget negotiation activities across awarded clinical trials.
jobs.description:
Description

The Site Contracts & Budget Manager provides operational leadership for site contracting and budget

negotiation activities across awarded clinical trials. The role is primarily accountable for contracting strategy,

Clinical Trial Agreement negotiation and execution, site budget negotiations, amendments, and resolution of

complex contractual and financial issues.

Working in close partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, the role translates proposal-stage

budget assumptions into effective study- and site-level contracting and negotiation strategies. Together, the

roles provide complementary leadership across the site budget and contracting lifecycle, with distinct primary

areas of accountability.

The Site Contracts & Budget Manager serves as a key contact and escalation point for sponsors, sites, and

internal stakeholders and provides functional guidance, training, and support to Site Budget & Contracting

personnel

Requirements

More specifically, the Site Contracts and Budget Manager must:

· Lead and manage Site Budget & Contracting staff, providing direction, coaching, development,

workload oversight, and support to ensure consistent quality and delivery across assigned studies.

· Oversee site contracting and budget negotiation activities across the portfolio, ensuring appropriate

resourcing, prioritization, quality, timelines, and escalation of risks or issues.

· Provide oversight of site contracting for awarded clinical trials, including Clinical Trial Agreements,

associated financial exhibits, amendments, negotiation parameters, and country-specific requirements.

· Establish and maintain contracting strategies, standards, and negotiation approaches that support

timely site activation while balancing sponsor requirements, organizational standards, site

expectations, and contractual risk.

· Serve as functional escalation point for complex or high-risk contract and budget negotiations,

providing guidance to team members and facilitating decisions with sponsors, sites, Legal Affairs, and

other stakeholders.

· Oversee the operational implementation of study-specific site budgets, including negotiation

parameters, approval pathways, exceptions, and escalation requirements.

· Translate proposal-stage budget assumptions into executable study- and site-level budget and contracting strategies.

· Collaborate with Legal Affairs, Project Management, Study Start-Up, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Operations, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure contracting and budget activities align with study requirements and operational plans.

  • Provide site contracting expertise during proposal development, including input on country-specific contracting requirements, anticipated timelines, institutional considerations, negotiation trends, risks, and resource needs.
  • Participate and/or support bid defence meetings, client presentations, and sponsor strategy discussions when site contracting, budget negotiation, timelines, or associated risks are relevant.
  • Monitor portfolio-level contracting and budget performance, identifying emerging risks, delays, capacity constraints, quality concerns, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Own and oversee the business assets supporting Site Budget & Contracting, including contract and budget templates, negotiation tools, country intelligence, guidance documents, trackers, reference materials, and other functional resources.
  • Ensure business assets remain current, fit for purpose, consistently applied, appropriately governed, and aligned with evolving operational and business needs.
  • Oversee the integrity, consistency, and usability of Site Budget & Contracting data across applicable tools, trackers, and systems.
  • Use contracting and negotiation outcomes to strengthen institutional and country intelligence and, in partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, inform future budget assumptions and benchmarks.
  • Lead functional process improvement initiatives to improve contracting and budget negotiation quality, efficiency, consistency, scalability, and stakeholder experience.
  • Support digital transformation and automation opportunities that reduce manual activities, strengthen controls, and improve the availability and quality of contracting and budget data.
  • Establish and monitor relevant performance indicators and use operational data to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities for corrective action or continuous improvement.
  • Ensure Site Budget & Contracting staff are appropriately trained and consistently apply relevant SOPs, processes, templates, tools, and quality standards.
  • Partner with senior leadership on resource and capacity planning, functional priorities, process maturity, systems and tools, quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement within the Site Budget & Contracting team.
  • Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Profile

  • B.Sc. or in a relevant field of study.
  • 5+ years of experience in clinical research, clinical trial budgeting, or related financial management roles within the pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO industry.
  • Strong negotiation and communication skills to engage with sponsors, external budget contacts, and internal stakeholders, serving as the escalation point to secure optimal study budgets.
  • Experience creating and maintaining budget templates tailored to global regions and therapeutic areas, ensuring scalability and consistency.
  • Collaborative mindset to partner with operational leads and ensure financial assumptions align with study design, operational strategies, and delivery plans.
  • Experience representing the organization in bid defense meetings and client calls, with the confidence to explain budget rationale and defend assumptions.
  • Technical proficiency to maintain pricing tools, cost databases, and budget models in collaboration with Finance and IT teams.
  • Leadership abilities to train and mentor junior specialists, provide guidance, and ensure team adherence to best practices.
  • Demonstrated success in partnering with senior team members to refine internal processes, drive efficiencies, and improve deliverables.
  • Strategic thinking to engage with leadership on process improvement initiatives, offering insights and recommendations that enhance operational excellence.
  • Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Flexible schedule
  • Vacation
  • Home-based position
  • Ongoing learning and development

About Indero

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

jobs.title: Junior Product Marketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: About Bask HealthBask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, product marketing plays an important role in connecting what we build with the businesses that use it. We value clear communication, a strong understanding of our customers, and the ability to turn complex product capabilities into practical value.

About the Role

We're looking for a Junior Product Marketing Specialist to support product marketing initiatives across Bask Health's software platform.

This is an early-career opportunity for someone who has some experience in marketing, content creation, customer research, or related work and wants to develop deeper expertise in product marketing.

You'll help communicate what Bask Health's products do, how they work, and why they matter to the businesses using our platform.

Bask Health brings together the tools entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses need to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform includes merchant tools, website creation, clinical and pharmacy workflows, AI-enabled features, analytics, and monetization capabilities.

As a Junior Product Marketing Specialist, you'll support the creation of messaging and marketing materials that help prospective and existing customers understand these capabilities.

You'll work with product marketing, product management, engineering, design, sales, customer success, and other internal stakeholders.

A major part of this role will involve turning product information into clear, accurate, and engaging customer-facing content.

You'll help develop feature descriptions, product overviews, launch announcements, presentations, and educational resources.

You'll work with product managers to understand new features, their intended use cases, and the problems they solve for customers.

You'll collaborate with technical stakeholders when additional product details are needed to ensure marketing materials accurately describe available functionality.

You'll support product launches by preparing content, organizing deliverables, tracking deadlines, and coordinating feedback.

You'll also help maintain existing product marketing materials as features evolve and new capabilities become available.

You'll conduct competitive research to understand how other SaaS, e-commerce, and healthcare technology companies position their products.

You'll help identify common messaging approaches, product differentiators, and customer concerns that may influence purchasing decisions.

You'll organize your findings into research summaries, comparison documents, and other resources that support product marketing decisions.

You'll partner with sales teams to understand common customer questions and help create materials that address them.

You'll also work with customer success teams to develop resources that support onboarding, feature education, and product adoption.

You'll help maintain product marketing documentation, messaging libraries, launch calendars, and content repositories.

You'll support website and landing page updates related to new product features and capabilities.

You'll have opportunities to contribute ideas for improving product descriptions, customer education, and marketing communications.

You'll also assist with reviewing product marketing performance through customer feedback, content engagement, launch results, and feature adoption data.

Because Bask Health operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll learn the importance of accurate product communication and appropriate internal review of clinical, pharmacy, or compliance-sensitive claims.

This role offers hands-on experience across multiple areas of product marketing while allowing you to develop stronger skills in messaging, research, content creation, and launch execution.

We're looking for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, comfortable working with different teams, and able to take ownership of assigned projects.

You should enjoy learning new software, asking questions, improving your work based on feedback, and finding clearer ways to explain complex products.

What You'll Do

  • Support product marketing initiatives across Bask Health's software platform.
  • Draft and update product descriptions, feature announcements, and customer-facing content.
  • Assist with developing product positioning and messaging.
  • Translate product functionality into clear customer benefits.
  • Support the preparation of product launch materials.
  • Track launch deliverables, timelines, and stakeholder feedback.
  • Collaborate with product managers to understand new features and updates.
  • Work with engineering and design teams to gather accurate product information.
  • Help create product overviews, presentations, and feature summaries.
  • Assist with developing sales enablement materials.
  • Support website and landing page content updates.
  • Conduct competitive research on SaaS, e-commerce, and healthcare technology platforms.
  • Organize competitive findings into clear summaries and comparison documents.
  • Research customer needs, purchasing considerations, and product use cases.
  • Gather customer insights from sales and customer success teams.
  • Help identify recurring customer questions and product objections.
  • Draft messaging that addresses common customer needs.
  • Support customer onboarding and product education initiatives.
  • Help develop tutorials, guides, and feature walkthroughs.
  • Assist with preparing product demonstrations and supporting materials.
  • Maintain product marketing documentation and messaging libraries.
  • Organize product information, research notes, and launch resources.
  • Support internal communications about product updates.
  • Review marketing materials for accuracy, clarity, and consistency.
  • Coordinate revisions and approvals with relevant stakeholders.
  • Assist with tracking product marketing performance indicators.
  • Analyze customer feedback and content engagement trends.
  • Recommend improvements to product messaging and educational materials.
  • Support additional product marketing projects as business needs evolve.

Requirements

  • Approximately 1–2 years of relevant experience in marketing, product marketing, content marketing, communications, or related work, including internships or contract experience.
  • Strong written communication skills.
  • Ability to create clear, well-organized marketing content.
  • Interest in technology, software products, and product marketing.
  • Basic understanding of marketing principles and customer messaging.
  • Ability to learn complex software functionality and explain it clearly.
  • Experience conducting research and organizing findings.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Good organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
  • Comfortable working with spreadsheets, presentations, and written documents.
  • Ability to communicate professionally with different stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Willingness to ask questions and seek clarification when needed.
  • Ability to incorporate feedback and improve work.
  • Comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to work independently on assigned projects.
  • Interest in understanding customer needs and business challenges.
  • Familiarity with B2B SaaS concepts or willingness to learn.
  • Ability to organize information and maintain documentation.
  • Strong initiative and ownership of assigned responsibilities.
  • Adaptability in a changing software environment.
  • Ability to learn new tools and processes quickly.
  • Commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in product marketing or SaaS marketing.
  • Internship experience at a software or technology company.
  • Familiarity with B2B SaaS business models.
  • Experience writing product descriptions or feature announcements.
  • Familiarity with e-commerce and direct-to-consumer businesses.
  • Experience using Shopify, website builders, or merchant software.
  • Experience conducting competitive or market research.
  • Familiarity with product launches and go-to-market activities.
  • Experience creating sales presentations or marketing collateral.
  • Familiarity with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, or similar productivity tools.
  • Experience using Notion, Figma, Canva, or related collaboration tools.
  • Basic understanding of customer acquisition and retention.
  • Familiarity with product analytics or marketing performance metrics.
  • Experience supporting customer onboarding or education initiatives.
  • Understanding of product-led growth concepts.
  • Familiarity with healthcare technology or telehealth platforms.
  • Interest in artificial intelligence and emerging software products.
  • Experience creating technical or educational content.
  • A portfolio of writing samples, marketing materials, or relevant projects.
  • Experience working in a growing technology company.

jobs.title: Regional Vice President, Enterprise Sales
jobs.excerpt: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.
jobs.description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job overview:

Omada Health is on a mission to inspire and enable people everywhere to live free of chronic disease. Employers are a critical part of that mission, sponsoring access to Omada's programs for their employees.

With 29 peer-reviewed publications demonstrating clinical and economic outcomes and a pay-for-performance business model, Omada is looking for a Regional Vice President, Enterprise Sales to grow our impact with the nation's largest self-insured employers.

This is an individual contributor role focused only on new-logo acquisition. You will own a territory of named enterprise prospects, typically employers with 10,000 or more covered lives, and be responsible for turning those accounts into Omada customers. Success requires a disciplined, account-based approach to prospecting, the patience and rigor to manage 6–12 month sales cycles, and full ownership of pipeline development. You will work closely with national and regional benefits consultants, health plans, and PBM partners while taking responsibility for creating opportunities—not relying solely on inbound interest, RFPs, or partner referrals.

Just as important, you are a skilled solution-based seller who leads with discovery rather than a product pitch. You build relationships across large, multi-layered organizations, uncover the business problems that matter to executive leaders, and understand how each employer makes decisions before recommending a solution. You translate those insights into a compelling, financially grounded business case that can withstand scrutiny from Benefits, HR, Finance, Procurement, and consultant advisors.

The ideal candidate combines drive and tenacity with strategic thinking, executive presence, sound judgment, and integrity. They are comfortable orchestrating complex enterprise buying processes, engaging C-suite and senior leaders, and sustaining momentum across long cycles with many stakeholders. They care deeply about their craft, their customers, and the relationships they build across the healthcare ecosystem.

This position reports to the National VP and works collaboratively across Omada's sales organization and cross-functional teams.

What You'll Do

Create and Develop Enterprise Pipeline:

  • Own new-logo business development for a territory of named enterprise prospects, typically self-insured employers with 10,000+ covered lives.
  • Build and execute a multi-year territory plan that prioritizes target accounts based on fit, timing, benefits strategy, and buying triggers such as consultant reviews, plan renewals, and vendor consolidation.
  • Develop account-level plans for priority prospects that map the organizational structure, key stakeholders, influencers, consultant relationships, and incumbent vendors.
  • Run a consistent, account-based prospecting cadence through executive outreach, benefits consultant relationships, and health plan and PBM partnerships.
  • Engage multiple stakeholders within each account to build early relationships, often well before a formal buying process begins.
  • Sustain pipeline-building activity across your named accounts while managing active, long-cycle opportunities toward closure.
  • Evaluate what is working, adapt your approach, and find new paths into accounts when initial efforts do not produce results.

Lead Discovery and Solve Executive-Level Problems:

  • Lead thorough, multi-threaded discovery to understand each employer's benefits strategy, workforce health priorities, cost drivers, point-solution landscape, and desired outcomes.
  • Move beyond surface-level requests to uncover underlying needs, quantify the impact of existing challenges, and identify the compelling reasons an enterprise would act.
  • Identify economic buyers, champions, decision criteria, decision process, and paper process early, and validate them throughout the cycle.
  • Develop tailored recommendations that connect Omada's multi-condition platform to the customer's specific needs, existing vendor ecosystem, and health plan or PBM arrangements.
  • Build a credible, data-driven business case, including ROI and cost-of-inaction analysis, and present it effectively to senior leaders across Benefits, Total Rewards, HR, and Finance.

Orchestrate Complex Enterprise Deals:

  • Own the full new-business sales cycle, from prospecting and qualification through consultant-led evaluations, RFPs, finalist presentations, contracting, and close.
  • Build and maintain mutual action plans with customers that define milestones, owners, and timelines across 6–12 month cycles.
  • Navigate enterprise buying processes that include procurement, legal, security and privacy review, data-sharing requirements, and health plan or PBM coordination.
  • Lead an internal deal team that may include solutions consultants, clinical and analytics experts, legal, implementation, and executive sponsors.
  • Partner with national and regional benefits consultants on account strategy, RFP responses, and finalist positioning.
  • Lead complex negotiations on pricing, performance guarantees, and contract terms in partnership with Deal Desk and Legal.
  • Ensure a clean handoff to Account Management and Client Success after close so new customers launch successfully.
  • Take accountability for pipeline development, sales execution, and quota achievement.

Maintain Accurate Sales Forecasting:

  • Maintain an accurate, up-to-date forecast grounded in customer engagement, confirmed next steps, and a clear understanding of each enterprise buying process.
  • Critically assess opportunity stage, close timing, and likelihood to close using evidence from discovery and deal progression—not optimism alone.
  • Apply a structured qualification framework, such as MEDDPICC, to inspect deals consistently over long cycles.
  • Proactively identify and communicate deal risks, stalled opportunities, and changes in timing, along with a plan to address them.
  • Keep CRM records current, including account plans, stakeholder maps, decision criteria, approval processes, and outstanding milestones.
  • Participate in regular pipeline and forecast reviews, clearly articulating what must happen for each opportunity to close and taking accountability for forecast accuracy.

What You'll Bring:

  • 5+ years of experience selling health and/or benefits solutions to large self-insured employers, including a track record of closing enterprise deals with organizations of 10,000+ employees or covered lives.
  • Demonstrated success winning new logos through proactive, account-based prospecting and sustained development of a named-account territory.
  • Experience managing long, complex sales cycles of 6–12 months or more with multiple stakeholders, formal evaluations, and RFPs.
  • Strong discovery skills, including the ability to uncover underlying business problems, quantify their impact, and understand the implications of leaving challenges unresolved.
  • Proven solution-based selling skills, with the ability to build a tailored, financially grounded business case for executive audiences.
  • Executive presence and experience engaging C-suite and senior leaders in Benefits, Total Rewards, HR, and Finance.
  • Established relationships with, and experience working alongside, national and regional benefits consulting firms.
  • Experience collaborating with health plan and PBM account teams in large employer accounts.
  • Experience negotiating enterprise contracts, including pricing, performance guarantees, and procurement and legal terms.
  • Experience using a structured qualification methodology (such as MEDDPICC) to manage pipeline and forecast accurately.
  • A consistent record of quota achievement and clear ownership of results.
  • Strong presentation, communication, and listening skills.
  • The self-direction to manage a named-account territory independently, prioritize effectively, and maintain momentum over long cycles.
  • Resilience when faced with rejection, stalled opportunities, or difficult sales cycles—and the judgment to adapt your approach.
  • Experience working in an emerging-growth company.
  • Bachelor's degree.

Location and Travel:

  • Candidates must reside in the midwestern United States; Illinois is preferred.
  • Ability to work Central Time business hours and support customers and partners across Central and Eastern time zones.
  • Willingness to travel approximately 25%–50% of the time within the territory, including onsite executive meetings, finalist presentations, and consultant meetings.

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus
  • Equity grants
  • Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP)
  • Remote first work from home culture
  • Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones
  • Generous parental leave
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)
  • 401k retirement savings plan
  • Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)
  • Mental Health Support Solutions
  • ...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!

  • Cultivate Trust. We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.
  • Seek Context. We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.
  • Act Boldly. We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.
  • Deliver Results. We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.
  • Succeed Together. We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.
  • Remember Why We’re Here. We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health: Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

jobs.excerpt: Why Join Intellia?  Our mission is to develop curative genome editing treatments that can positively transform the lives of people living with severe and life-threatening diseases.
jobs.description:
Why Join Intellia?

Our mission is to develop curative genome editing treatments that can positively transform the lives of people living with severe and life-threatening diseases.

Beyond our science, we live our four core values: One, Explore, Disrupt, Deliver and feel strongly that you can achieve more at Intellia. We have a single-minded determination to excel and succeed together. We believe in the power of curiosity and pushing boundaries. We welcome challenging thoughts and imagination to develop innovative solutions. And we know that patients are counting on us to make the promise a reality, so we must maintain high standards and get it done.

We wantall ofour people to go beyond what is possible. We aren’t constrained by typical end rails, and we aren’t out to just “treat” people. We’re all in this for something more. We’re driven to cure and motivated for change. Just imagine the possibilities of what we can do together.

How You Will Achieve More:

We are seeking a detail-oriented Senior QA Specialist to support document control and training administration within Quality. This hands-on role oversees the lifecycle of quality documents, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and personnel training programs within a GxP-regulated environment. This role ensures audit readiness, data integrity, and strict compliance with regulatory standard.

Hands-on Veeva experience is highly preferred, but not required.

This is a remote position.


Responsibilities:

Document Control

  • Format and quality-check SOPs, work instructions, forms, and other controlled documents for compliance with approved templates, formatting standards, and document management procedures.
  • Prepare documents and records in Veeva, maintain accurate metadata and version information, and route them through established review and approval workflows.
  • Coordinate with authors, reviewers, and approvers to resolve administrative issues and follow up on outstanding workflow tasks.
  • Process document issuance, effective dates, periodic reviews, revisions, obsolescence, and archival in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Verify required administrative information, attachments, and approval records for completeness; escalate discrepancies to the appropriate owner.
  • Maintain controlled templates and retrieve current or historical documents and records for business needs, audits, and inspections.
  • Track and manage the periodic document review process.
  • Improve documentation access and controls.
  • Develop, document and update quality policies, procedures and work instructions
  • Identify opportunities to streamline document lifecycle management, improve electronic workflow efficiency, and reduce manual administrative activities.

Training Administration

  • Administer training requirements, curricula, learner assignments, and associated records in Veeva in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Coordinate onboarding and role-change training assignments with managers and process owners.
  • Coordinate training assignments associated with new or revised controlled documents.
  • Monitor training completion, issue reminders, follow up on overdue assignments, and escalate unresolved gaps.
  • Maintain training completion records and generate training status reports and metrics.
  • Provide routine user support for document and training workflows; escalate technical or configuration issues to the designated system administrator.
  • Train GxP on documentation practices, quality standards, and system workflows.
  • Identify training gaps and coordinate with department heads to resolve compliance risks. Perform onboarding of new hires in relation to their training responsibilities and introduction to Veeva
  • Perform annual curriculum review
  • Facilitate the escalation of and resolution for issues connected to the learning management system and/or external tools

Quality Support and Continuous Improvement

  • Support audit and inspections by organizing and retrieving document control and training records.
  • Identify opportunities to improve document formatting, workflow turnaround, and training administration.
  • Support approved process improvements and procedure updates.
  • Manage assigned priorities independently, communicate deadlines, and promptly escalate potential compliance concerns.
  • Compile quality metrics, track document/training KPIs, and generate reports for management review.
  • Serve as a key Quality Systems resource for administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of electronic document management and LMS platforms within Veeva
  • Support implementation, configuration, testing, and enhancement of electronic Quality Systems workflows in collaboration with system owners, IT, Validation, and business process stakeholders.
  • Participate in user acceptance testing, change control assessments, procedural updates, and training activities associated with QMS system enhancements.
  • Support the preparation of audit/inspection responses, investigation documentation, and CAPA commitments related to assigned Quality Systems processes.
  • Promote a proactive culture of regulatory compliance, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.

About you:

  • Working knowledge of GxP documentation practices, controlled document lifecycles, training records, and data integrity principles for a commercial Quality Management System.
  • Hands-on proficiency in Veeva document control and training administration, including document and record routing, metadata, training assignments, and reporting.
  • Strong Microsoft Word skills, including styles, templates, tables, section breaks, pagination, headers and footers, and tracked changes.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PDF tools.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to process a high volume of documents and records accurately while managing competing deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently, troubleshoot routine workflow issues, and recognize when escalation is needed.
  • Clear communication skills and a collaborative, service-oriented approach to supporting internal users.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience. No specific certification required.
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology quality operations, document control, or training administration in a GMP environment.
  • Direct, hands-on Veeva experience is highly preferred.
  • Experience performing controlled document management and training administration is required.
  • Experience supporting audits or inspections and improving document or training workflows is preferred.
  • This role requires prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Occasional travel to the Cambridge, MA office may be required based on business needs.

EEOC Statement: Intellia believes in a diverse environment, and is committed to equal employment opportunity for all its employees and qualified applicants. We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. Intellia will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, and will continue to be accepted until the position is filled at which point the position will be taken down.

The base salary for this position is expected to range between $128,986.00 - $157,650.00 USD per year.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Planning & Performance (IBP)
jobs.excerpt: Finding the right place to grow your career isn’t (over) easy, so we’re here to help by sharing a few reasons why the grass is greener at Vital Farms.
jobs.description:
Finding the right place to grow your career isn’t (over) easy, so we’re here to help by sharing a few reasons why the grass is greener at Vital Farms. We think you’ll appreciate our focus on Conscious Capitalism, which drives business decisions that benefit all our stakeholders (leading to even better business results). You might be drawn to our innovative approach and refusal to settle for the “way things have always been done.” Or you could find it exciting to grow your skills while working for an industry-leading brand. Whether you’re into our values, our brand, or our egg-cellent puns, we hope you’ll join our Crew and help us change the world 108 square feet at a time!

At Vital Farms, we’re proud of the diverse communities we serve and the stakeholders who help bring our purpose to life. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative environment where every crew member feels valued. We see this as one of our greatest strengths - and your role is key to helping us build on it.

Your Role:

The Director, Integrated Business Planning (IBP) owns and facilitates Vital Farms’ established IBP process and advances its maturity and business impact. Partnering with next-level leaders (NLL) and functional leaders, this leader integrates commercial, operations, and financial plans across the rolling 36-month horizon to identify gaps and develop enterprise options. Together, they clarify tradeoffs and the cost and value of flexibility, align on one enterprise plan, and establish triggers to adapt.

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Operations Development, this role is an enterprise process owner, integrator, and facilitator. Functions own their plans, analyses, scenarios, recommendations, and execution: Demand Planning, within Sales Strategy, owns the demand plan; Supply Chain Planning (SCP) owns the integrated supply plan across the rolling 0–18+ month horizon; and Finance owns the financial outlook. The Director maintains IBP standards and governance, facilitates executive engagement, and supports business leaders in guiding discussions and decisions within agreed decision rights.

Following significant redesign and implementation, IBP has reached an intermediate level of maturity, with functional reviews in place. The mandate is to build on this foundation through deeper NLL engagement, clear functional ownership at each process step, and stronger scenario planning, performance measurement, and advanced analytics that create enterprise optionality and support timely, accountable decisions.

What You'll Do:

Lead and advance the IBP process

  • Own and facilitate the rolling 36-month Integrated Business Planning process, maintaining its standards, governance, and continued maturation.
  • Facilitate the monthly cycle across Product/Portfolio Review, Demand Review, Supply Review, Integrated Reconciliation, and Management Business Review, partnering with NLL so each forum produces decision-ready inputs, clear decisions, owners, and follow-through.
  • Advance standards, decision rights, inputs, outputs, KPIs, and meeting effectiveness while preserving what is already working and avoiding unnecessary process churn.
  • Govern the IBP maturity roadmap, including 2027 priorities for alignment, performance measurement, scenario planning, advanced analytics (including evaluation of AI), integrated planning across the rolling 36-month horizon, and connections to S&OE and AOP.
  • Partner with NLL and functional owners to define preparation, analysis, recommendations, presentation, and follow-through at each process step, so reviews are function-owned while IBP provides governance, integration, and enterprise consistency.
  • Continuously improve the process based on business performance, participant feedback, and evolving enterprise needs.

Integrate functional plans into one enterprise view

  • Create connectivity across Commercial, Operations, Finance, strategy, and AOP without duplicating the planning work owned by those functions.
  • Partner with Sales Strategy and Demand Planning to bring a clear, assumption-based demand plan and its risks and opportunities into IBP.
  • Partner with SCP to bring the integrated supply plan, constraints, farm and network implications, options, and recommendations into Supply Review. SCP owns the rolling 0–18+ month supply plan; IBP owns cross-functional integration and enterprise decision forums across the rolling 36-month horizon.
  • Partner with Finance to reconcile operational and commercial assumptions to the financial outlook and quantify the value, risk, and tradeoffs associated with scenarios.
  • Connect the strategic plan, AOP, commercial plan, and operations plan so longer-range commitments and near-term actions reinforce one another.
  • Maintain an integrated view of assumptions, gaps, risks, opportunities, and decisions rather than acting as the owner of every underlying number.

Enable decisions through scenarios, optionality, and strong facilitation

  • Partner with functional owners to turn complex planning inputs into focused, decision-ready executive conversations.
  • Identify material gaps to strategic and financial targets, clarify the decision required, and ensure the right owners develop fact-based options.
  • Facilitate functional development of practical base, upside, downside, and gap-closure scenarios, making tradeoffs across growth, service, capacity, supply, cost, margin, inventory, cash, and risk visible.
  • Distinguish operational planning decisions from enterprise tradeoffs: functional teams own their plans and recommendations; IBP enables decisions when choices span functions, materially affect targets, or require executive alignment.
  • Facilitate constructive debate, surface misalignment early, and prevent short-term exceptions from consuming the rolling 36-month IBP agenda unless they create material longer-term implications.
  • Enable functional leaders to bring concise, financially grounded narratives to leadership and executive forums that clarify what changed, why it matters, the options considered, the recommended path, and the decision required; bring their perspectives together into a coherent enterprise view.
  • Build enterprise optionality by clarifying the cost and value of flexibility and establishing triggers to commit, act, or adapt as conditions change.

Strengthen governance, accountability, and execution

  • Ensure decisions made through IBP translate into coordinated action and measurable outcomes.
  • Define and uphold decision rights, escalation thresholds, calendars, templates, and quality standards across the IBP cycle.
  • Maintain a transparent decision and action log, including owners, timing, expected value, retained options, review triggers, dependencies, and closure.
  • Ensure approved decisions flow back into demand, supply, financial, and execution plans, with clear connections to SCP and S&OE where applicable.
  • Define and govern business-performance and planning-health KPIs across the IBP cycle; monitor plan performance, bias, adherence, risk realization, and decision effectiveness, and use insights to improve both the process and future choices.
  • Lead through influence across NLL, senior leaders, and functional teams, creating shared accountability for enterprise outcomes.

Build sustainable IBP capability

  • Develop the organizational understanding and behaviors required for IBP to operate as a business management process, not a planning department.
  • Coach NLL, functional review owners, and participants on effective plan ownership, assumptions, scenarios, risk/opportunity thinking, and decision preparation.
  • Clarify the interfaces among IBP, Demand Planning, SCP, Finance, AOP, and S&OE so work occurs once, at the appropriate level, with clean handoffs.
  • Promote a shared-facts culture, using data to challenge assumptions while balancing analytical rigor with practical business judgment.
  • Partner with functional and data teams to evaluate fit-for-purpose tools, advanced analytics, and AI use cases based on value and feasibility, strengthening decision quality without allowing technology to lead the process.

What Success Looks Like:

  • IBP forums consistently focus on material risks, opportunities, scenarios, and enterprise decisions across the rolling 36-month horizon rather than detailed short-term execution.
  • Demand, supply, and financial plans are visibly connected, with differences in assumptions identified and resolved.
  • NLL and functional leaders consistently prepare and present decision-ready plans, alternatives, and recommendations; the IBP team owns integration, process integrity, and decision effectiveness.
  • Decisions are timely, fact-based, financially grounded, clearly documented, and translated into updated functional plans and execution.
  • Repeatable scenarios clarify tradeoffs, the cost and value of flexibility, and triggers to act or adapt, surfacing options before lead times or commitments limit choices.
  • Leaders trust the process as the primary forum for aligning the enterprise plan and managing delivery against strategic targets.
  • IBP maturity advances through governed KPIs and measurable improvements in decision quality, accountability, cross-functional alignment, and plan performance.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Strategy, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience; master’s degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience across Supply Chain, Finance, Strategy, Commercial Planning, Operations, or related CPG functions, with meaningful leadership of IBP, S&OP, enterprise planning, or comparable cross-functional processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to mature an established IBP or S&OP process in a CPG, food, manufacturing, or similarly complex operating environment, including governance, facilitation, scenario planning, and change leadership.
  • Deep understanding of the distinct roles and interfaces among Demand Planning, Supply Chain Planning, Finance, AOP, S&OE, and IBP.
  • Experience with planning horizons that bridge near-term execution and longer-range strategic choices, ideally 18–36 months.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect operating assumptions and decisions to growth, margin, cash, service, capacity, inventory, and risk.
  • A facilitator-coach approach, with exceptional facilitation and communication across functions and leadership levels; able to simplify complexity and enable business-owned recommendations and decisions.
  • Strong analytical and systems thinking, paired with the willingness to work in the details when needed.
  • Experience with planning technology, scenario modeling, data visualization, and business intelligence; experience partnering on AI-enabled planning is helpful.
  • Adept at influencing without direct authority and building accountability across senior, cross-functional stakeholders.
  • This position is remote within the United States, with an estimated travel requirement of 10–20% based on business needs.
  • You’re no hero – You know the power of teamwork and celebrate the work of others before your own.
  • You give a sh*t – You believe in acting like an owner and making Vital Farms a place to be proud of.
  • You raise the standards – You know growth can be hard, but you strive to improve yourself and others each day.
  • You can walk in someone else’s boots – You seek to understand other’s viewpoints and think that you get to better answers by sitting on the same side of the table.
  • You don’t walk on eggshells – You’re not afraid to leave the bullsh*t behind and have honest conversations.
  • We recognize that talent comes in many forms. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. You may have strengths we haven’t yet considered!

What We Bring to the Table:

  • A fast-paced, energetic, remote environment with passionate people who are leading a movement to bring ethically produced food to the table.
  • Competitive pay and benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision, and Paid Parental Leave, just to name a few).
  • Generous retirement contributions: 401(k) + 3% Contribution from Day 1.
  • Free eggs, along with friends and family discounts.
  • Fun team SWAG that will make you the talk of the town.
  • Professional development opportunities and an amazing team dedicated to your growth.

At Vital Farms, compensation decisions are dependent upon a variety of factors, which may include, but are not limited to, skill level, experience, education, training, market demands, and business needs. A reasonable estimate of the current starting annual base salary for this position is $170,000 - $190,000. Please keep in mind that hiring at the maximum end of the range would not be typical in order to allow for potential continued future salary growth.

#VFPJ

Who We Are:

Vital Farms, a Certified B Corporation, offers a range of ethically produced foods nationwide. Started on a single farm in Austin, Texas, in 2007, Vital Farms became a national consumer brand that works with 600 family farms and is the leading U.S. brand of pasture-raised eggs by retail dollar sales. Vital Farms’ products, including shell eggs, butter, hard-boiled eggs, and liquid whole eggs, are sold in over 24,000 stores nationwide.

Vital Farms’ ethics are exemplified by its focus on the humane treatment of farm animals and sustainable farming practices. In addition, as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation, Vital Farms prioritizes the long-term benefits of each of its stakeholders, including farmers and suppliers, customers and consumers, communities and the environment, crew members, and stockholders. In short, we exist to improve the lives of people, animals, and our planet through food.  

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

To fulfill Vital Farms mission of bringing ethically produced food to the table, we’re committed to building teams that reflect diverse perspectives and lived experiences. We believe that when all crew members feel valued and respected, they bring their best ideas forward - fueling innovation, belonging, and shared success. We strive to create a welcoming environment rooted in equal opportunity and encourage individuals from all backgrounds and experiences to apply.

To that end, we make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, and business need. Vital Farms does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender and gender identity, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, marital status, age, national origin, citizenship status, military or veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Ready to Join Us?

Together, we’re cultivating an environment where every Crew member can thrive, grow, and know they’re part of something bigger - improving lives through ethical food.

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, we’d love to hear from you! Even if you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply - you might be exactly what we need!

Next Steps:

Shortly after you complete your application, you'll receive a follow-up email elaborating on any potential next steps in our process. If you don't immediately receive said follow-up email, we would highly encourage you to check your spam filter!

In order to fulfill Vital Farms mission to “bring ethically produced food to the table,” we seek to build teams that leverage diverse perspectives to create a welcoming and innovative environment that is committed to the principles of equal employment opportunities.

Staying Safe During Your Job Search

At Vital Farms, we care deeply about the people interested in joining our Crew. That includes helping protect candidates from fraudulent recruiting activity and creating a hiring experience that is safe, respectful, and transparent.
Unfortunately, job scams are becoming increasingly common. We encourage all applicants to stay vigilant throughout the hiring process and verify opportunities directly through our official careers page.

We are committed to treating every candidate with fairness and respect and to creating a hiring experience worthy of your trust.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Overview

Deriva Energy is a leading Independent Power Producer in the US renewables market, with over 6.5GW of operating or under construction wind, solar and storage projects across the country. Formerly the division of Duke Energy, Deriva is now backed by Brookfield Renewable and is poised for dynamic growth across its wind, solar, and storage portfolios. Join a dynamic team committed to excellence and innovation who envision a future of energy independence using resilient, carbon-free generation. We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and the opportunity to make a significant impact on the rapidly evolving renewable energy industry. Deriva empowers customers with innovative clean energy solutions that strengthen communities and serve future generations.

Position Summary

The Solar Planner-Scheduler develops and supports maintenance plans and resource-based schedules supporting a 694 MW portfolio, comprised of 4 Texas sites. This role is expected to be expanded, as Deriva extends operations to new operating sites (Texas/Midwest). This role ensures maintenance work is properly planned, resourced, scheduled, and execution-ready to improve reliability, workforce utilization, and operational performance.


Working closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Warehouse, contractors, and site leadership, the Planner-Scheduler coordinates maintenance activities, identifies resource constraints, and supports safe, efficient execution of work.

This position will be Remote (TX), with a preferred location near the following cites; Austin, Midland, San Angelo, Waco. Highly qualified candidates, based in the United States, may be considered for remote locations outside of Texas.

Main Responsibilities

Work Planning & Readiness

  • Develop detailed work packages including scope, labor estimates, procedures, parts, tooling, equipment, vendor support, and safety requirements.
  • Conduct field walkdowns when needed to validate scope, site conditions, and resource requirements.
  • Review equipment history, fault trends, and previous work orders to optimize planning quality.
  • Ensure all work is fully planned and execution-ready before scheduling.

Scheduling & Resource Coordination

  • Maintain a rolling 6-12 week maintenance schedule across multiple sites and work groups.
  • Coordinate activities among Operations, Maintenance, High Voltage teams, Engineering, contractors, vendors, and support organizations.
  • Balance priorities based on equipment criticality, risk, workforce availability, materials, outages, budgets, and operational needs.
  • Continuously adjust schedules and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce downtime, and optimize labor utilization.

Materials, Tooling & Vendor Readiness

  • Ensure required parts, materials, tooling, vehicles, and equipment are available before scheduled work.
  • Coordinate with Supply Chain, Warehouse, and site personnel to resolve shortages and resource constraints.
  • Escalate potential issues early to prevent schedule impacts.

Work Management Systems (Maximo)

  • Serve as the area subject matter expert for Maximo and mobile work management tools.
  • Create and maintain work orders, job plans, preventive maintenance programs, standard work packages, labor estimates, and material requirements.
  • Support backlog management, work prioritization, schedule compliance, and continuous improvement of work management processes.

Performance & Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor schedule execution and analyze planning and labor variances.
  • Identify causes of delays and execution challenges, including parts, tooling, vendor, resource, or scope issues.
  • Use historical performance data and technician feedback to improve future planning accuracy and scheduling effectiveness.
  • Track and communicate key planning and scheduling metrics to leadership.

Reliability, Compliance & Safety

  • Support risk-based maintenance prioritization and equipment reliability initiatives.
  • Coordinate required clearance, switching, and tagging activities.
  • Assist with NERC and other regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Promote strong safety, environmental, and procedural compliance throughout the planning and scheduling process.

Basic Qualifications

Job Summary

Senior Systems Engineer – Clinical NLP Research Support

Aptive Resources is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to support a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Research and Development (ORD) research study at the Durham VA Health Care System.

The study is the largest gene-by-environment genome-wide interaction study (GEWIS) of suicidal thoughts and behaviors to date, drawing on data from the Million Veteran Program (MVP). Its objective is to discover new, replicable gene-by-environment interactions that increase Veterans' risk, and its long-term goal is to inform screening and intervention strategies that reduce suicide and suicidal behavior among Veterans. The Senior Systems Engineer will support this work by turning VA electronic health record (EHR) clinical text into validated, analysis-ready data for the study team.

The ideal candidate will have significant experience developing artificial intelligence/super intelligence (AI/SI) methods for clinical or EHR text evaluation and leading the full technical lifecycle of population-scale text-processing pipelines in a healthcare or research environment, such as VA.

This is a part-time (20 hours/week), 100% remote position. It is currently funded through September 29, 2027 under the current contract period of performance, with potential for extension into the next option year based on contract continuation and program needs.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop methods and infrastructure, and refine natural language processing (NLP) and large language model (LLM) approaches, to identify predictor variables for suicidal thoughts and behaviors in VA electronic health record (EHR) clinical notes, under the direction of the study team.
  • Build and maintain custom tokenization and text-processing pipelines that run at population scale across the Million Veteran Program (MVP) cohort.
  • Extract and validate phenotypes (suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and related exposures) for the study's gene-by-environment analyses.
  • Prepare, document, and transfer analysis-ready datasets to the study's statistical genetics team.
  • Manage technical lifecycle activities, including code version control, testing, documentation, and reproducibility within the VA research computing environment.
  • Ensure all work complies with VA privacy and information security requirements for protected health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII).
  • Troubleshoot pipeline performance, scalability, and data quality issues, and recommend and implement improvements.
  • Coordinate with the Principal Investigator and study team and provide regular progress updates against project milestones to support completion within the grant period.
  • Prepare technical documentation, workflow documentation, and handoff materials.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, data science, informatics, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years of experience in computer systems engineering, software development, data engineering, or technical implementation.
  • Experience with AI/SI methods development, including developing LLM models, for EHR text evaluation within a federal research environment.
  • Experience with the technical lifecycle of this type of research, including custom tokenization and population-scale work.
  • Experience with programming and data pipeline development.
  • Experience working with protected health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII) in accordance with VA privacy and security requirements.
  • Ability to work independently in a part-time, remote role while meeting project deadlines.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and research stakeholders.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a public trust clearance.
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States.

Desired Qualifications

  • Significant experience developing NLP or LLM methods for VA.
  • Experience supporting research studies, particularly in genomics, and familiarity with programs like the Million Veteran Program.
  • Experience with transformer-based models, model fine-tuning, or custom tokenizer development.
  • Experience developing or validating computable phenotypes, including chart review or annotation workflows.
  • Experience with GPU-based or high-performance computing environments.
  • Familiarity with mental health or suicide prevention research.
  • Experience with version control, technical documentation, and reproducible workflows.
  • High degree of professionalism, discretion, and mature judgment in handling sensitive information.

Physical Requirements

Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for extended periods, use a computer keyboard and mouse, and communicate verbally and in writing. The employee may occasionally need to stand, walk, bend, or lift up to 15 pounds. jobs.description:
The Principal Product Manager, Clinical Data Analytics, will play a pivotal role in shaping Tendo’s data-driven solutions by translating clinical and financial-focused activities into actionable insights that support patients, providers, and health systems. This individual will help define product strategy and functional requirements for analytics offerings, leveraging deep expertise with healthcare coding systems (ICD-10, DRG, CPT) and payer/provider data workflows. Specifically, this role will help define data requirements and business logic to:

  • Measure provider-level clinical quality from claims data.

  • Analyze the relationship between quality, price, and market share for health procedures.

  • Identify missing comorbidities from EHR patient records.

This role requires a strong balance of technical acumen, healthcare domain knowledge, and product management experience. This person will work closely with engineering, clinical informatics, and customer-facing teams to deliver data solutions that improve decision-making, enhance operational efficiency, and support Tendo’s marketplace growth. Under Tendo’s AI-First R&D model, this role operates as a Product Engineer with domain strength, owning features end-to-end from discovery through release, with AI as the first author at every stage.


About TendoMake an impact—join our team!

We’re a fast-growing, mission-driven company building a culture that enables teams and individuals to thrive. Our team-driven culture and rapid growth have earned us recognition as one of Forbes’ Top Startup Employers for 2024, 2025, and 2026. Led by an experienced and proven team, we live by our values and are always on the hunt for motivated people with diverse experiences and backgrounds to help us improve the care journey for patients, clinicians, and caregivers by creating software that provides seamless, intuitive, and user-friendly experiences.

If you like working with innovative technologies and want to be part of a growing team that will help transform the healthcare experience, we encourage you to apply today!

Job LocationSalt Lake City, UT

Responsibilities

Ability to critically evaluate published quality methodologies and translate them into production-grade product functionality.
